Sports.title: The not-so-obvious chance Leclerc missed to usurp Verstappen
Sports.content:
When Charles Leclerc had a better start than Max Verstappen and claimed the inside line for Turn 1, many in the media centre thought the Monegasque should have held his ground to take the lead.

However, Verstappen was on the outside, on the normal racing line that offered slightly more grip, and the Dutchman was prepared to take every risk. Verstappen had already told Autosport a day earlier that second or third place in the drivers' championship would mean nothing to him and that he simply wanted to go all-in for race victories.

In other words, Verstappen was willing to risk everything, although that was not even the main reason why Leclerc was unable to complete the move. The reference points drivers use under braking – such as the 150-metre and 100-metre boards – are on the right-hand side approaching Turn 1, but Leclerc could not see them because he was alongside Verstappen.

The Ferrari driver had to choose his braking point by instinct and tried to judge it as well as possible. As a result, he does not regard it as a missed opportunity, adding: "I would have done exactly the same."

No regrets in that respect, then, although Leclerc admits that he did let an opportunity to pass Verstappen slip away a few laps later.

Verstappen appeared to be managing his pace in the opening stages to preserve his tyres, but the four-time world champion revealed in the post-race press conference that this was not entirely a deliberate choice.

"We had a few laps with some deployment issues, so that's where Charles actually almost got me into Turn 7."

Verstappen managed to keep the lead into Turn 1, despite Leclerc's better launch off the line Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Verstappen was not getting all the electrical power at the points where he needed it, something Arvid Lindblad at Red Bull's sister team Racing Bulls – which uses the same power unit – also complained about.

"Yeah, I also had issues with the PU, which we're trying to look after. I was getting driven past on the straights and the engine braking was really bad, which wasn't easy to drive", Lindblad said.

For Verstappen, the problem was limited to deployment issues in the opening stages of the Singapore Grand Prix, but Leclerc believes he should have taken advantage of them.

"There were a few opportunities in the first three laps when Max had the deployment issues, but I always thought that it was a one-off, so I wasn't really using my battery, which maybe was a mistake", Leclerc admitted.

Every time Verstappen was slow on the straights, the Ferrari driver thought it would be the last time, meaning he did not anticipate the problem recurring or adjust his own deployment strategy accordingly. By the time the issue occurred again, Leclerc could no longer react.

"When I was realising that he had no power at the end of the straight, I couldn't do anything. It was too late for me to use my power."

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The question, however, is whether it would have made any difference to the final result. Track position is crucial at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, and in that scenario Leclerc would not have had to spend so long running in dirty air. On the other hand, he acknowledges that Verstappen was simply too strong and that Red Bull managed its tyres better.

"I don't know if it would have changed much. Of course, for the first stint it would have helped, but I think eventually they just had too much pace for us."

Leclerc made another attempt in the closing stages with a different strategy and a second stop under the virtual safety car, but a second win of the season, following his triumph at Silverstone, ultimately proved beyond reach.

"I’m happy, but not super happy. I mean, second place is a good result considering the tendency that we've had lately, where we were lacking just a little bit of pace.

"I feel like, particularly in qualifying yesterday, we had strong pace. Today in the race, Max had a bit more pace than we did, which was expected, but maybe we were a little bit closer than what we expected.

"It was a cool race and I believed in it until the very end, but unfortunately it wasn't quite enough."

Nevertheless, it was enough to secure Leclerc's first podium finish since the summer break and his fifth overall this F1 season.

Sports.title: The hidden factor that gives Verstappen and Red Bull extra hope for 2027
Sports.content:
With two victories in the last three Grands Prix and a deficit of just 0.196 seconds in Baku, Verstappen and Red Bull are firmly back at the front in Formula 1. The resurgence has understandably come too late to play a meaningful role in the title fight, although Verstappen now has a top-three finish in the drivers' championship in his sights.

Verstappen trails Lewis Hamilton by just eight points after the Singapore race weekend, while Russell is only 17 points ahead of the Dutchman. In other words, finishing runner-up in the championship is a realistic prospect.

When Autosport asked whether Verstappen is already starting to worry about 12 December – when the annual FIA gala takes place in Shanghai – a smile appeared on his face.

"Is that the prize-giving ceremony? Well, I was really ill last year! But we'll see what happens."

A second- or third-place finish in the final standings would not mean anything to Verstappen, however, as he told the Dutch media in the Singapore paddock. After the extremely difficult start to 2026 and the turnaround that followed, such an outcome might carry more significance than usual, but Verstappen does not see it that way.

"No, because ultimately you're not winning. You're not becoming world champion, and that's the only thing that matters to me."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The aspect of 2026 that gives Verstappen the most confidence

While the title is out of reach this season, Red Bull's resurgence does provide confidence for next year.

"The most important thing is to look at where we were at the beginning of the season and where we are now", Verstappen said, referring to the fact that Red Bull was still fighting Haas and Alpine in China and Japan.

"All the upgrades that have been introduced on the car since then, and also the problems we had with certain parts of our car, we've managed to solve all of that. That's very important heading into next year.

"When you see that some teams still have doubts about certain aspects of their new upgrades, everything is working for us, and that's a real positive."

Verstappen has previously explained that certain limitations of the 2026 car can no longer be eliminated, meaning more fundamental changes will still be needed for next season's car.

Asked by Autosport whether the development direction is already 100% clear in that respect as well, and whether it gives Verstappen confidence, he replied:

"You never know fully. It's always very difficult to say that with things you're developing now that have never actually existed in real life, only on drawings.

“But everything we've introduced on the car this year has worked. That's very positive, and hopefully we can use that for next year."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

What's the latest on Red Bull's long-awaited new wind tunnel?

Verstappen also brought up another, more hidden factor that could help Red Bull as 2027 progresses:

"Of course, we'll also have a new wind tunnel at our disposal next year. That's a separate matter, but naturally we hope it will work properly and help us as well."

The wind tunnel Red Bull currently uses is the oldest on the F1 grid. During his time as team principal, Christian Horner repeatedly described the wind tunnel as “a Cold War relic” and said working with the 70-year-old facility near Bedford was like looking at “two different watches”, highlighting how the correlation between the wind tunnel and on-track performance had failed more than once.

The fact that correlation has proved accurate in 2026 is therefore not something to be taken for granted, although Verstappen added that the new regulations and the dimensions of the cars may be helping as well.

"Those earlier problems might also have been partly down to the width and length of the car [and what you can replicate with the model]. Of course, we have different cars now, but the most important thing is that we'll be able to use the new wind tunnel next year."

Verstappen acknowledged that the new wind tunnel cannot yet be used for the initial development of the RB23 – after all, that development process is already underway – but it can be used for further development of the car throughout the season. That will still be crucial, as the second year under these regulations is also set to feature an intense development battle.

Pierre Waché previously told Autosport that the wind tunnel should be operational in early 2027, possibly in February, as Red Bull indicated in Singapore. However, the exact timing during the first quarter of 2027 will still depend on factors such as calibration, ensuring that Red Bull can have complete confidence in its new facility.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Track Verstappen’s best result Hamilton’s best result Bahrain International Circuit 1st 1st Jeddah Corniche Circuit 1st 1st Albert Park 1st 1st Suzuka 1st 1st Shanghai International Circuit 1st 1st Miami International Autodrome 1st 6th Circuit Gilles Villeneuve 1st 1st Monaco 1st 1st Autodromo do Algarve 2nd 1st Silverstone 1st 1st Red Bull Ring 1st 1st Spa-Francorchamps 1st 1st Hungaroring 1st 1st Monza 1st 1st Madring 2nd DNF Baku City Circuit 1st 1st Istanbul Park 2nd 1st Singapore 1st 1st Circuit of the Americas 1st 1st Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 1st 1st Interlagos 1st 1st Las Vegas Strip Circuit 1st 2nd Losail International Circuit 1st 1st Yas Marina 1st 1st

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Sports.title: Social Media: Mekies extends contract to lead Red Bull until 2031 | Brief
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence in its team principal Laurent Mekies by extending his contract to run the team until 2031.

Mekies took over from Christian Horner in charge of the team last year. Horner had run Red Bull since it entered F1 in 2005.

Under Mekies, Red Bull rebounded from a poor start to last season. From over 100 points behind, Max Verstappen came within two points of retaining his drivers’ championship title in one of the closest ever finishes to a world championship.

This year, in the team’s first season with its own power units designed in conjunction with Ford, Red Bull has won the last two grands prix.

Sports.title: Verstappen says Red Bull’s car was “scary” to drive early in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has made huge progress with a car which felt “scary” to drive early in the season, says Max Verstappen.

The four-times world champion has won the last two grands prix in a row and also took victory in the sprint race in Singapore last week. The team’s form has improved significantly since the beginning of the season, when Verstappen only reached the podium once in the first seven rounds.

Verstappen spun out of the British Grand Prix suffered costly spins in qualifying at the Red Bull Ring and Hungaroring as the team struggled to get on top of its car. However their most recent upgrades have transformed its performance.

“The car definitely felt a lot nicer from Baku onwards,” said Verstappen. “It’s just been a lot more balanced. Then naturally, of course, when you can compete a bit further up front without having too many issues with the car compared to the beginning of the year, where it was actually sometimes a bit scary to drive, that makes it a lot nicer.”

Verstappen finished a close second behind George Russell in Baku. He qualified only eighth but was in contention for pole position until his final lap was compromised by a yellow flag.

He has been undefeated since then and expects to remain competitive over the final rounds. “We’re not in a championship fight, and that’s why I think ’til the end we’ll just try to have a good time and try to add more podiums and hopefully a few wins.”

It is the second time in as many years that Red Bull has made a breakthrough with a troublesome car in the second half of a season. “Two completely different cars as well, with the regulations,” Verstappen noted. “Also two completely different problems.

“We had to find lap time. Plus, of course, also this year with the engine side of things, I think for everyone it’s been sometimes a bit complicated to get the most out of it.”

Red Bull needs to ensure they begin next year in better shape, said Verstappen.

“From race one to now, I think we’ve gained a lot of experience. Of course, we’re still not where we want to be, but I guess everyone will say the same thing.

“But we have learned so much and definitely also on the car side have fixed a lot of our weaknesses. We just need to keep improving, keep learning this year that so we can apply that also into next year.”

Sports.title: Spotlight: Cadillac already has better facilities than Mercedes, says Bottas | Brief
Sports.content:
Cadillac remain yet to score a point in their first season in Formula 1 but Valtteri Bottas says their progress is clear to see.

“We are definitely seeing an improvement somewhere every weekend,” he told the Financial Times. “It’s not necessarily in the results yet, but it’s in how we operate as a team in different areas.”

Bottas scored all 10 of his grand prix victories for Mercedes. He drove for the world champions between 2017 and 2021.

Cadillac is based partly at Silverstone, a short distance from Mercedes’ Brackley factory. Asked whether his new team’s facilities are better than the world champions’, Bottas replied: “I would say so.”

Sports.title: Devin Haney Claims Shakur Stevenson Wanted Rehydration Clause
Sports.content:
Update: Devin Haney fired back at Shakur Stevenson, stating he initially accepted 145 pounds before Stevenson vanished for days and tried sneaking in a rehydration clause.

“You’re cap.. I agreed to 145 u went missing for days. Tried to put a rehydration clause on me. I wasted 6 months negotiating with you,” Haney posted on X. “I been negotiating with u since i was gonna sign to Zuffa. Yall did every thing for this fight not to happen even tried to throw Keyshawn in my way.”

Haney brings a crucial detail into public view. His original stance was 145 pounds with zero weight limits on fight morning. If Stevenson demanded a ceiling on Haney rehydrating after the weigh in, that altered the deal completely.

That explains Haney shutting down the catchweight talk. Trimming down two extra pounds while keeping the freedom to bulk back up on fight night is completely separate from accepting strict secondary limits. Haney skipped over Stevenson’s claim that an attorney formally demanded 147 pounds, but his message makes his anger obvious.

For Haney, who already had to dry himself out to shave two pounds off the 147 welterweight limit, that restriction is brutal. Capping Haney at 155 on Saturday morning prevents him from drinking freely, forces him to go to bed dehydrated, and leaves him depleted inside the ring.

That is why Haney walked away. Offering the two-pound concession at 145 was already a compromise.

Devin Haney Has Reasons to Reconsider Shakur Catchweight

Shakur Stevenson claims Devin Haney pulled out of their agreed 145-pound catchweight to demand the full 147-pound welterweight limit, blowing up a deal that looked locked down earlier this month.

Shakur has plenty of reason to be furious. Still, Haney can always rethink whether draining himself below welterweight makes sense against a slick target who rarely gets hit cleanly.

“At the 11th hour, after agreeing to 144 and then 145, DeeHoe had his lawyer email and say that he would only fight at 147. Big waste of everybody’s time,” Shakur posted on X.

Haney originally offered 145 with no rehydration limits, which Shakur took on October 8 with a quick reply: “145.0 U GOT A DEAL.” If Stevenson is telling the whole story, Haney backed off the exact compromise he put on the table.

Fans will call him out for it, but Haney does not have to sign off on terms that leave him depleted in the ring. Two extra pounds below welterweight might sound like nothing from the couch, but that extra pull can easily ruin a camp.

Stevenson is stepping up from 140 to take a shot at Haney’s WBO welterweight belt. Haney can legitimately question why he should drain his body for a challenger whose defensive mastery already makes for a nightmare night at the office.

Haney holds the chips here. He carries bigger commercial pull, so Stevenson is hardly his only ticket to a monster bag. Sitting back to see what happens between Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez gives him another massive payday with far less hassle.

Nobody has seen the lawyer’s email yet, and Shakur never explained what prompted the change. His anger makes complete sense after shaking hands on a public deal, but Haney has to protect his physical edge while weighing the bigger options waiting for him.

Once a fighter shows weakness on the scales, the other camp smells blood and starts picking at the money.

Catchweight concessions always shift the psychological leverage. If Haney drops down to 145 just to accommodate Shakur moving up from 140, Shakur immediately feels like the A side dictating terms. From that vantage point, Shakur starts pushing for an even split or demanding parity he has not earned at the box office.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Replaces Shakur Stevenson Atop Ring Rankings
Sports.content:
Stripping Shakur Stevenson of the top spot at lightweight was long overdue. The Ring finally bumped William Zepeda to number one, updating the board to reflect reality since Shakur departed for junior welterweight.

Shakur hasn’t stepped into the ring at 135 pounds since his 2025 scrap with Zepeda. He snatched the WBO junior welterweight belt off Teofimo Lopez in January. Keeping him perched above fighters who actively compete in the weight class makes zero sense.

Leaving a division means stepping aside for the next man up, whether Shakur likes it or not. He got the official win over Zepeda, sure. That win shouldn’t grant him lifetime ownership over a division he completely walked away from.

That bout was much tighter than the lopsided scorecards indicated anyway. Zepeda relentlessly marched forward for twelve complete rounds, pressing Shakur hard without offering any real breathing room. On my scorecard, that fight was a draw. Shakur landed cleaner single shots, but those flashes never created the massive margin the judges turned in.

Now Zepeda sits atop an exciting lineup featuring Abdullah Mason, Floyd Schofield, plus Andy Cruz. This crew brings serious offensive firepower, giving 135 pounds a fresh identity beyond Shakur’s ultra-defensive fencing routine.

Every single one brings a distinct look. Zepeda drowns opponents in relentless volume. Mason pieces together crisp, heavy combos. Schofield loves trading shots in the pocket. Cruz flashes elite technical timing, bringing an offensive arsenal that belongs against the division’s best.

Getting these contenders inside the ropes together is the real challenge now. Deep rankings do not mean much when promotional walls keep top talent apart.

Shakur earned his respect at lightweight, but holding the crown requires actually fighting there. The 135-pound scene has plenty of momentum to move forward, giving Zepeda the green light to take over the division.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Wanted $1.73 Million for Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Liam Paro’s reported $1.73 million asking price was more than Devin Haney wanted to pay for a welterweight unification. The figure offers an explanation for why talks failed to produce a fight between the two champions.

Paro would have brought his IBF belt into a contest with WBO champion Haney. That gave Haney an opportunity to collect another title, but the sides still needed to agree on the cost of making it happen.

Australian journalist Peter Badel described Paro’s financial expectations in comments reported by EverythingBoxing, which credited @JaiMcAllisterx.

“Liam Paro — a little bit has gone quiet there. Look, I’ve been talking to his team. They’ve been a little bit frustrated. They’re trying to get the right fight at the right price for Liam,” Badel said, as quoted by EverythingBoxing. “I’m told he was seeking around 2.5 million Australian dollars [$1.73 million US] for a fight against Haney. Haney didn’t want to pay him that amount.”

EverythingBoxing identified the comments as being eight days old. Badel’s account gives Paro’s reported asking price without revealing Haney’s offer or how far apart the sides were.

Haney’s position involves more than choosing his next opponent. He operates Devin Haney Promotions and has worked through co-promotional agreements, giving him a business interest in the cost of putting a fight together.

Another championship gives Haney something to pursue, but his side must also decide whether an opponent’s price fits the event’s budget. Paro has his own title to bring to negotiations and a financial return he wants from risking it.

The reported $1.73 million request alone does not establish that Paro priced himself out. Equally, declining that figure does not establish that Haney wanted to avoid him.

The missing piece is the counteroffer. Without knowing what Haney’s side offered, it is difficult to judge whether Paro’s expectations prevented an agreement or whether the available money simply fell below his price.

Sports.title: Rico Verhoeven Accepts Deontay Wilder Fight Offer
Sports.content:
Rico Verhoeven has accepted an offer to fight Deontay Wilder on December 11, potentially adding another heavyweight bout to the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff.

Wilder’s response is still outstanding, and the terms need to be negotiated. However, Verhoeven has made his willingness clear as he looks to continue boxing after his stoppage loss to Oleksandr Usyk.

“I can’t confirm just yet,” Verhoeven told talkSPORT. “What I can tell you is that they offered me the fight. They offered me Deontay Wilder. I said yes.” “The details need to be talked about still. But for that, I’m waiting on a response. So, if there’s a yes from the other side, it’s going to happen.”

Verhoeven did not identify who made the offer. His comments introduce another possible opponent for Wilder, who had been linked with a fight against Jai Opetaia on the same card.

Wilder would give Verhoeven an opportunity to turn the praise he received against Usyk into a victory over an established heavyweight. Going deep into a fight with Usyk earned him attention, but beating Wilder would give him something firmer to build on.

There is an obvious danger in treating Wilder as a faded name to collect. His right hand still gives Verhoeven a reason to be careful. Yet Wilder’s reduced activity and hesitant offense in recent performances could allow the Dutchman time to settle into the fight.

Verhoeven also made clear that he intends to remain in boxing after considering several offers.

“I want to make a statement,” he said. “I want to show that … I am able to transition into the sport of boxing.”

Peter Fury remains in his corner, and Verhoeven is already looking beyond the proposed December appearance. He hopes Joshua beats Fury because he wants that fight himself.

“I hope that Anthony Joshua’s winning that fight because then I’m next for him.”

Beating Wilder would give that ambition a stronger foundation. First, Wilder needs to accept.

Putting Wilder against Verhoeven spares Jai Opetaia a bizarre heavyweight detour that threatened to derail his cruiserweight meeting with David Benavidez. That alone makes it slightly more tolerable than the initial rumor, but it remains a carnival booking.

Wilder has looked completely spent for years. At 40, his trigger is hesitant, his balance is compromised, and the reflex to pull the trigger on his right hand has eroded. Grinding past an aging Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision did not erase the one-sided beatings he took against Joseph Parker, Fury, or Zhilei Zhang.

Verhoeven, 37, proved his toughness by surviving into the eleventh round against Oleksandr Usyk, but surviving is not contending. He is an elite kickboxer with a tiny boxing resume, still learning basic ring craftsmanship under boxing rules.

Sticking two aging names together with mismatched pedigrees belongs on the preliminary streaming portion of the broadcast, not sharing equal billing right beneath Fury against Joshua. It caters to novelty rather than sport.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Rates Dubois Wardley Rematch Even
Sports.content:
Frank Warren still views Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley as a 50-50 fight heading into Saturday night at the O2 Arena in London. Even though Dubois won their violent clash in May, Wardley dropped him in the first and third rounds, proving his power can alter the course of the bout instantly.

Dubois weathered that storm to secure the stoppage, yet those early visits to the canvas give Wardley massive confidence that he can flip the script. The real challenge for Wardley will be finishing the job if he gets Dubois in trouble again.

“I just feel that either of them can win. I think it’s still an even-money fight,” Warren told talkSPORT. “Daniel will go as favorite because he’s probably … got more experience as amateur as well as pro.”

Surviving clean bombs once does not guarantee Dubois can take them a second time. At the same time, reckless aggression could cost either man dearly.

“You’ve got to remember he called for this rematch,” Warren said of Wardley. “It was a brutal fight in May, and here we are now, and it’s on, and he believes that he can win it.”

Warren believes victory hinges on establishing the jab instead of hunting for wild knockout blows right away. For Dubois, a sharp jab keeps Wardley on the outside and stops him from landing cold early.

“For me, the key to this fight is getting behind the jab,” Warren said. “Not looking to lead with big punches, to actually go out and try and … jab and then let your shots go.”

Both heavyweights know what to expect after their first battle. The winner will be the man who made the right adjustments and capitalizes on them first. Neither fighter is built to play it safe, which is why Warren expects another explosive finish before the final bell sounds. Dubois proved his resilience, Wardley proved his firepower, and both step into the ring knowing one clean shot can end it.

When promoters preach boxing fundamentals and patience for a high-profile rematch, they are usually trying to protect their fighters from another grueling brawl. The problem is that fans are paying for fireworks, not a tactical chess match.

“They know each other’s strengths and weaknesses,” Warren said. “It’s who’s learned from the last fight and who can exploit what he’s learned.”

If Dubois and Wardley actually listen to Warren and spend 36 minutes trading cautious jabs from ring center, public reaction will be brutal. Paying premium pay-per-view prices on DAZN just to watch two sluggers neutralize each other behind the lead hand is the exact opposite of what made their May fight thrilling.

“I don’t think the fight’s going to go the distance, whatever happens.”

The thin undercard makes that risk even worse. Here, there is zero safety net. If the headliner devolves into a safety-first sparring session, the whole broadcast will disappoint, and the backlash from paying customers will land squarely on Warren.

Sports.title: Ermal Hadribeaj Taunts Sebastian Fundora Ahead Of Upset Bid
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora gave Ermal Hadribeaj an icy glare during Thursday’s final presser at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Tension spiked when Hadribeaj aimed an imaginary sniper rifle directly at the champion’s chin.

Fundora kept his cool. The towering titlist didn’t swat the hand away. He didn’t shove the challenger. He simply stared him down, leaving the theatrics entirely to the Albanian contender.

Many boxing fans dismiss Saturday’s DAZN broadcast as a total mismatch. They might be forgetting history. Brian Mendoza knocked Fundora out cold in 2023. Erickson Lubin battered him. Tim Tszyu landed heavy leather on him. Those past fights prove the champion absorbs massive punishment when his defense gets sloppy.

The height gap between the two southpaws is ridiculous. DAZN’s faceoff clip showed the eight-inch difference clearly. Hadribeaj stands five feet ten inches tall, forcing him to point his fake rifle skyward toward Fundora’s 6’6″ stature.

Landing real leather will prove vastly tougher than gesturing on stage. Hadribeaj has to slip past huge reaching punches. He must escape clean counters. Closing distance against the champion is tricky because Fundora actually loves trading in tight phone booths.

That exact habit offers Hadribeaj his clearest path toward an upset. Fundora constantly surrenders his height by planting his feet inside. Shorter opponents suddenly find themselves in prime position to connect clean shots.

Mendoza exploited that flaw with a brutal left hook. Hadribeaj hasn’t demonstrated that kind of world class power against elite fighters yet. Still, writing off the challenger ignores the defensive gaps Fundora regularly presents.

The champion stayed composed on stage. Bringing that same discipline into Saturday night keeps the challenger outside, preventing Hadribeaj from getting the messy close-quarters brawl he desperately craves.

Hadribeaj’s taunting is unlikely to get Fundora to fight with reckless anger. Fundora has been through heated build-ups before, taken real damage in wars with Lubin and Tszyu, and generally keeps an even temper outside the ring. At the presser, he watched the sniper pantomime without flinching or retaliating.

The interesting part is that Hadribeaj probably does not even need to make Fundora angry to get the fight he wants. Fundora naturally surrenders his eight-inch height advantage without any emotional prompting. His default setting is to march forward, plant his feet, and throw uppercuts and hooks in a phone booth.

He gives up range as a matter of style, not because his temper got the better of him. That was how Mendoza caught him, and that was how Tszyu landed punishing overhand rights before the cut changed the dynamic.

Hadribeaj’s hurdle is what happens when he actually gets inside. Fundora is lethal in close quarters, throwing sharp uppercuts that chew fighters up as they try to stay under his reach. If Hadribeaj spends energy looking for one theatrical, loaded-up counter shot against a guy who throws heavy volume in the pocket, he risks getting overwhelmed by the sheer number of punches coming back at him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney-Shakur Stevenson Purse Clash Could Sink Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson finally agreed on 145 pounds, but dividing the revenue could scuttle their bout before either man steps into the ring.

Talks have reached a critical point, putting the targeted November 28 date in Atlanta in real jeopardy. Settling on a catchweight gave both camps a clear target. Splitting the revenue creates a deeper rift because it hinges entirely on personal market valuation.

Haney’s November 28 date allows almost no room for further haggling. Just over six weeks remain on the calendar, meaning both boxers require signed contracts right now to launch proper training camps. Every day squandered bickering over percentages pushes that target closer to collapse.

Haney has every right to challenge an even split. He already proved his drawing power as a headline attraction. Agreeing to parity would concede commercial ground that his team believes Shakur has yet to earn.

Backing from Turki Alalshikh changes the financial landscape. Deep financial support guarantees a massive overall purse, but funding a guarantee is not the same as generating revenue through paying customers. Haney’s side will almost certainly demand terms that honor that distinction.

“A potential fight between Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson is facing obstacles,” Mike Coppinger reported, adding that negotiations were “reaching a critical stage to keep this fight alive.

Coppinger did not reveal the figures being discussed, but if Shakur wants an equal or larger share, that could be where the talks are getting stuck.

Haney holds the cards here. Devin has options, commercial value, and a willing audience. Shakur cannot afford another inactive stretch where he sits around polishing belts while the division moves on without him. If he lets his ego dictate both the scale and the purse split, Haney will simply walk, leaving Shakur with an empty calendar and nobody to blame but himself.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia-Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

“Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are now in advanced talks to fight in the first quarter of 2027, sources tell. Expect this welterweight title fight to happen next. And it’s a big one,” said Coppinger on X. “I believe the Garcia-Teo fight will happen regardless of the WBA’s ruling here. Catterall could end up being elevated.”

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Ghana News.title: Mahama reaffirms commitment to private investment and industrial growth
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for private investment and industrial growth.

The President made the remarks during a working visit to the Bright International Industrial Zone, where he cited the US$2.62 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) recorded in 2025 as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Ghana.

Mr Mahama expressed optimism that the rollout of the New Economy Policy would further strengthen the country’s investment prospects and enhance its attractiveness to investors.

He highlighted the importance of maintaining investor confidence and creating favourable conditions for private-sector investment to support industrial development.

The President’s visit to the Bright International Industrial Zone emphasised the Government’s focus on encouraging private investment and promoting industrial growth as part of its broader economic agenda.

Ghana News.title: ‘We have been used and dumped’ – NDC’s James Agbey warns over grassroots neglect
Ghana News.content:
An operative of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), James Agbey, has warned that the party risks alienating its grassroots supporters unless government appointees address concerns about neglect and a lack of economic opportunities.

In a statement dated Friday, October 16, Mr Agbey accused appointees of overlooking activists and cadres who worked to secure the party’s return to power in the 2024 elections.

“The feeling out there at the base is that ‘we have been used and dumped’,” he said.

Mr Agbey claimed that many party activists were struggling with unemployment and financial hardship, while some appointees were prioritising relatives and close associates over those who supported the party during its years in opposition.

“Everything seems to have changed after the elections. Appointees are now prioritising their families and close allies, some of whom were not even part of the struggle,” he alleged.

He said the concerns required practical intervention rather than occasional handouts or promises of future support.

“All that these party activists are asking for is opportunities to be able to fend for themselves,” he stated.

Mr Agbey urged government appointees to engage with the party’s support base and take concrete steps to address their concerns.

He warned that unresolved grievances could weaken loyalty and lead dissatisfied activists to turn against the government in a future election.

“Our support for the NDC must not be taken for granted,” he cautioned.

The statement did not provide figures to substantiate his claim that the party’s support base was dwindling or identify the appointees accused of favouring relatives and associates.

Mr Agbey nevertheless maintained that the leadership needed to act urgently to prevent growing frustration from damaging the party’s electoral prospects.

“I call for urgent action or we will have ourselves to blame come the electioneering season,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Ghana defender Marvin Senaya begins training ahead of comeback
Ghana News.content:
Black Stars fullback Marvin Senaya has returned to light training on grass as he aims to return to competitive action following a muscle injury sustained during the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Senaya suffered a hamstring injury during Ghana’s Round of 32 clash against Colombia in July and has been out since the new season commenced.

The injury has forced the Ghanaian fullback to miss the opening seven league matches for AJ Auxerre.

His return to on-pitch running shows progression in his recovery. However, a definite return to competitive action has not been confirmed.

Senaya was a standout player for Ghana during the 2026 World Cup, earning praise for his performances during the campaign.

His eventual return to match fitness will be a bright spot for Auxerre, while the Black Stars will also hope to utilise the defender for upcoming international fixtures once he full recovers.

Ghana News.title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari urges women leaders to build strong support networks
Ghana News.content:
Senior Presidential Advisor and Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has urged women in leadership to surround themselves with people who will support their growth, defend them against unfair treatment and offer honest advice.

In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, she reflected on a discussion with former Electoral Commission Chairperson Charlotte Osei at the Obaasima Conference, where the challenges women encounter in leadership featured prominently.

Ms Bawah Mogtari said the conversation reinforced the importance of having a dependable support system in workplaces where women’s abilities and achievements are often questioned.

She said a genuine support network should go beyond public expressions of solidarity to include people willing to speak up against injustice, offer constructive criticism and celebrate the progress of others without feeling threatened.

Such relationships, she noted, can make a significant difference in how women navigate the pressures of leadership.

Ms Bawah Mogtari said the Obaasima Conference should provide a platform for women to share their experiences, learn from one another and develop meaningful connections.

She stressed that while leadership can be difficult for women, having trusted people to rely on can make the journey more manageable and rewarding.

Ghana News.title: Bawumia engages GUTA over import duties, VAT and rising business costs
Ghana News.content:
Former Vice President and New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer for the 2028 elections, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has held talks with the Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA) on challenges affecting traders, including high import duties, rising demurrage charges and the cost of doing business.

In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, Dr Bawumia said executives and representatives of GUTA outlined concerns over high import duties, the reported increase in VAT for informal sector operators to 20%, limited access to EXIM loans, high shop rents and goodwill payments, as well as foreign nationals taking over aspects of the retail trade.

He described the engagement as productive and said the association also presented proposals to address some of the challenges.

The discussions also focused on how Ghana could move from dependence on imported goods towards local production. Dr Bawumia said he and the traders explored incentives that could encourage businesses to manufacture more goods locally, potentially creating jobs and expanding opportunities for Ghanaian businesses.

He thanked GUTA for the engagement and the ideas it presented, saying the discussions had provided useful insights into the difficulties facing traders.

The meeting forms part of conversations on possible policy measures to improve the business environment, ease operational pressures and support domestic production and private-sector growth.

Ghana News.title: Fuel prices begin to fall as Star Oil cuts petrol to GH¢16.45
Ghana News.content:
Some oil marketing companies (OMCs) have begun reducing fuel prices at the pumps as the second pricing window for October takes effect.

Star Oil reduced its petrol price from GH¢16.64 to GH¢16.45 per litre, effective 8am on Friday, October 16, 2026.

Other OMCs have told JoyBusiness they intend to review their prices, although some say they will monitor competitors before making adjustments.

While motorists could benefit from lower petrol and diesel prices, users of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) face a projected increase of more than 18%. The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies expects LPG to sell at about GH¢20.60 per kilogramme.

Reasons for the adjustments

The Chamber attributed the projected price movements to developments in the international petroleum market, exchange-rate pressures, and recent government interventions.

According to its report, average crude oil prices rose by 2.03% to US$126.73 per barrel for the October 16 pricing window.

The Chamber linked the increase to renewed supply concerns, citing uncertainty over a proposed US-backed energy ceasefire involving Ukraine and fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia amid the conflict with Iran.

Despite the rise in crude prices, refined petroleum products recorded mixed movements. International LPG prices increased by 7.77%, while diesel and petrol prices fell by 6.68% and 3.93%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the cedi depreciated by 1.61% against the US dollar, reaching an average bank rate of GH¢11.8222 between September 26 and October 11, 2026.

The Chamber said the local currency had lost more than 11% against the dollar since the beginning of the year, with seasonal import demand and higher energy costs continuing to exert pressure.

The weaker cedi is expected to limit how much of the decline in international petrol and diesel prices is passed on to consumers.

Competition and the NPA’s price floor

Some OMCs say competition will influence the timing and extent of their price adjustments.

However, their pricing decisions must also comply with the National Petroleum Authority’s minimum price requirements.

Market information available to JoyBusiness puts the petrol price floor at GH¢16.09 per litre and the LPG floor at GH¢13.87 per kilogramme.

These floors represent minimum selling prices, not the pump prices that every company must charge. Actual prices may therefore vary among OMCs.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod supplies banks with US$282m in weekly forex sales
Ghana News.content:
Sammy Gyamfi, GoldBod CEO

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) says it sold US$282 million to commercial banks through its foreign exchange (FX) sales programme on Tuesday, October 13, and Thursday, October 15, 2026, as part of efforts to increase dollar supply to Ghana’s domestic market.

In a statement, the Board said US$197 million was sold on Tuesday, followed by an additional US$85 million on Thursday. GoldBod explained that the transactions were conducted through its digital GoldBod GoFX platform to make foreign exchange earned from Ghana’s gold resources available to participating commercial banks.

GoldBod said the programme is backed by Section 2(b) of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which provides for the Board to supply foreign exchange to the country.

According to the Board, participating banks submit requests for US dollars through the platform, with allocations made under the real-time monitoring of the Bank of Ghana.

The Board reiterated that the arrangement constitutes spot FX sales rather than forex trading. It explained that it sells dollars earned from its gold operations to commercial banks in exchange for cedis, which are then used to finance its gold purchases.

GoldBod said the supply of dollars to commercial banks helps businesses access foreign currency for imports, international payments and other legitimate obligations.

The Board added that improved FX availability could help ease pressure on the cedi and imported costs, while supporting market stability and the financing of its gold purchasing operations.

Ghana News.title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari says Obaasima Conference should help women connect and learn
Ghana News.content:
Senior Presidential Advisor and Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has called for the Obaasima Conference to serve as a space where women can openly discuss their leadership experiences, learn from one another and build relationships that strengthen their professional and personal development.

In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, she reflected on a conversation with former Electoral Commission Chairperson Charlotte Osei, whose account of the challenges of being a woman in leadership prompted her to consider the value of shared experiences and mutual support.

Ms Bawah Mogtari said the discussion highlighted the pressures women may face, from rumours and workplace prejudice to colleagues who question their ability to handle responsibilities.

She said creating opportunities for women to discuss such experiences openly could help them find practical ways to navigate difficult working environments and encourage one another.

She identified the importance of finding a supportive circle of people who will offer honest counsel, stand against unfair treatment and celebrate each other’s achievements.

According to Ms Bawah Mogtari, that spirit of connection and solidarity should be central to the Obaasima Conference, enabling women not only to exchange ideas but also to build lasting networks of support.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
