Ulasi said he challenged that optimism, questioning what the opposition had done on the ground to demonstrate that Atiku would win.

“When he was coming up, we had an emergency meeting somewhere (with Atiku). I think everybody was there, and governors were saying, ‘You have won, you have won already.’ I said, ‘You must be jokers,’” he recalled.

According to Ulasi, he was asked to leave the meeting after challenging the claims, but returned after Atiku called him back.

“I said, who has won? That Atiku sitting down here, which election has he won against Tinubu? What have we done on the ground to show that Atiku will win?” he said.

Ulasi noted that Tinubu eventually won the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the opposition should learn from that experience rather than repeat its mistakes.

“And we went to that election. What happened? Tinubu won. And we again in another cycle of election. Like you rightly said, the opposition is so fragmented now, worse than it was in 2023,” he said.

Assessing the political landscape, Ulasi said defeating Tinubu would require an extraordinary effort if the opposition remained divided.

“So, only God will answer that question, if there is some divine process going on. But as things are on the ground, it will take some magic for anybody to stop Tinubu. I can tell you that,” he said.

World.title: NAF deploys pumping machines to recover crash wreckage in Ondo
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigerian Air Force has engaged community leaders and residents of Igbokoda, Ondo State, over concerns that ongoing aircraft recovery operations could affect their water source.

The engagement was led by the Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command, Air Vice Marshal MC Ekwueme.

During the engagement, the AOC acknowledged the concerns raised, assured the community of the Nigerian Air Force’s (NAF) commitment to addressing the issues, and appreciated the people for their patience and cooperation during this difficult period.

The AOC also engaged personnel at the recovery site, where significant progress is being made despite the challenging terrain and difficult underwater conditions.

Multiple pumping machines have been deployed to remove water from the area surrounding the crash site, a critical step towards accessing the main wreckage, which remains submerged and deeply embedded in the riverbed.

A statement by Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of Public Relations and Information, said, “This painstaking process requires sustained effort, specialised technical support and careful coordination to advance the recovery operations safely and effectively.

‘The NAF recognises the profound grief of the bereaved families and the concerns of Nigerians awaiting further progress. While the difficult riverbed conditions and the depth at which the wreckage lies make the operations complex, recovery personnel continue to work diligently towards accessing the main wreckage, with due regard for their safety and the dignity of the victims.

“The ongoing deployment of pumping equipment represents an important step towards facilitating the next phase of recovery.

Beyond the recovery efforts, the CAS has reaffirmed the NAF’s commitment to supporting the bereaved families through this painful period.

He assured that all applicable entitlements, including benevolent funds, scholarships for eligible children and other approved welfare benefits, would be duly processed.

The NAF recognises that its responsibility to the affected families extends beyond the recovery operations and remains committed to providing the necessary support with compassion, dignity and a deep sense of duty.

The service continues to engage with affected families and has established a dedicated helpline at Headquarters Nigerian Air Force to facilitate access to timely and appropriate information.

The NAF acknowledges the environmental concerns raised by the Igbokoda community and remains committed to engaging with residents and addressing the issues through appropriate channels.

The service appreciates the community’s cooperation and the dedication of personnel and partner agencies working under challenging conditions and will sustain recovery efforts, support the bereaved families and provide verified updates on significant developments as the operation progresses.

World.title: Shooter kills teacher, three children at US elementary school
World.content:
Candles and flowers are seen at a makeshift memorial outside the Silver Rail Elementary School following a shooting in Bend, Oregon, on October 15, 2026. Three children and one teacher were shot dead at an elementary school Thursday in the northwestern US state of Oregon, police said, adding that the assailant was a 16-year-old who was killed by an armed bystander. (Photo by Payton Bruni / AFP)





A teenager shot and killed three children and a teacher on Thursday at an elementary school in the US state of Oregon, police said, adding the assailant was later killed by an armed bystander who pursued him into the building.

Officers rushed to Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, a city of about 100,000 in the nation’s northwest, after reports of a shooter on campus on Thursday afternoon.

The three children who died on the scene were aged five, eight and 11, said Bend police chief Mike Krantz. Another child and a teacher were being treated for critical injuries after the shooting.

The United States, where firearms are readily available, has a long and painful history of gun violence, with thousands of people killed every year. It has the highest rate of gun-related deaths among all developed nations.

People gathered in the city’s Drake Park on Thursday evening for a candelight vigil remembering the victims.

“I’m in total complete shock, and scared and sad,” said Betsy, who did not give her last name. She spent around 10 minutes contemplating a circle of candles and flowers.

“It’s awful, but it also has brought people together,” she told AFP.

Krantz, the police chief, told journalists that the department first learned of an active shooter after a call from a person who reported being shot at multiple times by a person carrying a long gun.

Dozens of emergency calls then reported that a shooter had entered the school and all law enforcement in the area were called to the scene, the chief added.

Officers arrived at 1:02 pm local time (2002 GMT) within minutes of the calls, he said.

“Moments later, an officer reported that the suspect had been shot by a community member who had seen the suspect enter the school and pursued him into the school and engaged him,” Krantz said.

“Our officers entered the building and confirmed the suspect was dead.”

One seven-year-old and one 54-year-old teacher with critical injuries were transported to a local hospital, he said.

The police chief said the investigation was in its early stages, but told the press conference it appeared “the shooter had forced their way into the school by shooting at locked doors.”

He added that the 16-year-old shooter was a Bend resident.

– ‘Unthinkable tragedy’ –

Between 400 and 450 children attend Silver Rail Elementary, where more than 40 staff work, according to a police spokesperson.

After a lockdown, Bend-La Pine School District said law enforcement was escorting students in buses to a separate location, where families could reunite with their children.

The district’s superintendent, Steve Cook, tearfully called the day’s events “an unthinkable tragedy.”

“We are heartbroken. We are horrified. This is the kind of thing you hear about in other places, and pray that it never happens here,” he told reporters.

Parents were anxiously waiting at the site near a church, where Drew Sharp, the father of a fifth grader, the highest grade in the school, told CBS News: “I have faith that he’s okay and that he’ll be alright.”

Children were disembarking from the bus youngest to oldest “which makes sense,” Sharp said, but “it’s just more time waiting.”

Friday classes at schools across the district along with activities and athletic events were canceled, Bend-La Pine said in a statement.

The elementary school is approximately 170 miles (270 kilometers) southeast of the city Portland. It serves primary-age students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

– ‘Cannot keep accepting this’ –

The deadliest school shooting in US history took place at Virginia Tech on April 16, 2007, when South Korean student Seung-Hui Cho killed 32 people and wounded 17 others before taking his own life.

There have been more than 360 mass shootings in the US so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines a mass shooting as four or more people shot.

“Our hearts are with the terrified children and the families anxiously waiting to hear that their loved ones are safe,” GIFFORDS, a gun safety organization, said on X.

“We cannot keep accepting this as a fact of life.”

Thursday’s shooting was followed by a painfully familiar chorus of calls for action on gun control, pleas that have resulted in little meaningful change.

In the face of decades of massacres, the powerful US pro-gun lobby has given millions of dollars to primarily conservative politicians in a successful bid to keep gun laws loose.

“They’re killing our babies. Shredding our kids with lead. Forcing us to live in fear,” said Janelle Bynum, an Oregon congresswoman, in a statement.

“This continues to happen,” she said later, speaking on CNN. “And it seems as if the adults don’t care.”

World.title: 2027: CSO Coalition Cautions Enugu Guber Candidates, Demands Issue-Based Campaigns
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Coalition of Civil Society Groups for Good Governance (CCSGG) Thursday cautioned governorship candidates in Enugu State against inflammatory politics and smear campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging them to present verifiable development agendas to the electorate.

The coalition, which said it comprises over 52 civil society organisations committed to promoting accountability and good governance, stated this at a world press conference themed: “Enugu State and the Politics of 2027: Putting the Record Straight.” in Abuja

Addressing journalists on behalf of coalition, Comrade Okpanachi Jacob, said the group intervention became necessary following the controversy surrounding the incident at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu, on October 10, 2026, involving supporters of the National Democratic Congress (NDC).

He noted that the group investigated the matter after statements attributed to the NDC governorship candidate, Sir Christian Chinyeaka Ohaa, and others, which linked the Enugu State Government to the incident.

The coalition described the suggestion that a political rally was to be held at an international airport as deeply concerning and inconsistent with established standards for aviation security.

It noted that according to accounts released by the Enugu State Government and the Enugu State Police Command, the NDC had publicised a “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport, was advised to secure approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), but allegedly proceeded without such approval, leading to a confrontation when security personnel restricted access.

The coalition therefore posed five questions to the NDC to answer in public interest, stating:

“Did the party obtain formal approval from the appropriate federal airport authorities for the gathering? If approval was obtained, will the party publish it for public scrutiny? What instructions were given to party members concerning access to the airport? Why was a large political gathering planned for a sensitive federal facility? What credible evidence directly connects Governor Peter Mbah or any identified state official to the confrontation?

“Freedom of association and peaceful assembly are constitutional democratic rights. However, those rights must be exercised lawfully and responsibly. Political enthusiasm does not override aviation security,” the coalition said.

It urged politicians to desist from disseminating misleading information, stressing that airports are sensitive federal facilities whose security and operations must not be compromised by partisan activities.

The coalition said Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah is not above criticism, noting that citizens, opposition parties and journalists have the right to question his policies, scrutinise public expenditure and demand transparency. However, it said criticism must be based on facts and not on demonisation or allegations unsupported by evidence.

“Accusation without evidence is not accountability. It is political blackmail capable of inflaming passions, misleading the public and undermining the peace and security of Enugu State,” the group said.

The group stressed that opposition status does not confer immunity from regulations governing airports, political gatherings and public order. Adding: “It said all political parties must notify appropriate authorities of major public activities, comply with lawful security requirements and ensure members do not engage in violence or destruction of public property.

It also called on security agencies to remain professional, impartial and proportionate, ensuring a level playing field for all parties while respecting citizens’ rights to peaceful assembly.

The coalition warned against importing thugs, arming supporters, spreading unfounded security alarms or manufacturing confrontations for propaganda, urging security agencies to investigate reports of attempts to recruit armed persons ahead of 2027.

World.title: Nigerians Can Grow Capital, Assets Through Cooperatives, Says Adesope
World.content:
Nigerians can grow their capital, assets and income through cooperative societies, the newly elected President of The Bodija (Ibadan) Unique Cooperative Investment & Credit Society, Mr Olufemi Adesope, has said.

Adesope urged managers of cooperative societies to encourage members to save and invest more consistently while developing attractive investment products and expanding their investment portfolios to ensure continuous growth in capital, assets, income and members’ return on investment.

He made the call while assuming office for the 2026/2027 Cooperative Year at the society’s ninth Annual General Meeting held at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan.

Describing his new responsibility as a call to duty, Adesope said, “We must build on our successes, learn from our experiences and deliberately position Unique Cooperative Society for greater heights.”

Speaking on the theme of the AGM, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he called for a shift from dependence on traditional cooperative activities to identifying viable businesses, property investments, community projects and other sustainable income-generating opportunities.

“The Society should continuously ask: ‘What new opportunities can create additional value for our members?’” he said.

Adesope also stressed the need to build relationships with credible financial institutions, professional organisations, businesses, technology companies, other cooperatives and development institutions.

He called for continuous training of members and leaders in financial literacy, investment, entrepreneurship, leadership and digital skills.

On the need to adapt to developments in the financial world, the new president advocated the digitalisation and automation of the society’s operations.

He said this should cover member registration, savings, loans, investment monitoring, communication, reporting and performance tracking.

“Technology should make the Society faster, more transparent, accessible and efficient,” he said.

Adesope, while commending the Board of Trustees, including the society’s foundation president and past president, Mr Olusegun Sanni and Mr Gbolahan Arogundade, respectively, for their guidance, wisdom and continuing support, said the new leadership would maintain the highest standards of transparency, prudent financial management, risk control and accountability.

He also called for measurable annual targets for membership, savings, investments, income, assets and member benefits, with regular performance reviews to ensure progress.

“ Our goal must not merely be to preserve what we have built, but to continuously grow, improve and create greater value for every member,” he said.

Also speaking at the AGM, the keynote speaker, Professor Sulaiman Adesina Yusuf of the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Ibadan, advised people seeking steady financial growth to join cooperative and credit societies and pool resources with others.

Yusuf, a professor of agricultural economics, urged members to participate regularly in the growth process and allow their collective investments to grow over time.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Building Bridges, Empowering Members: Cooperatives in the Digital Age,’ he challenged cooperative leaders to avoid the pitfalls of the past by embracing digital transformation to encourage more people to join their societies.

However, he cautioned that the human element of cooperative societies must not be overlooked in the drive towards digitalisation.

“Let us be honest with each other: a digital notice is not the same thing as meaningful participation. An app cannot manufacture trust,” he said.

Yusuf explained that technology could strengthen transparency and accountability by enabling members to access their balances, decisions and records.

“What it can do, if we build it honestly, is make trust visible: a balance a member can check, a decision a member can read, a record a member can request.

“Technology can support accountability. It cannot take responsibility for it. That responsibility still belongs to us, the leadership and the membership of this cooperative.”

World.title: Hamzat: African Govts, Private Sector Must Increase Investment in Digital Infrastructure
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

The Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, has demanded of African governments and the private sector to increase investment in digital infrastructure, stressing that the continent’s major challenge in technological development is not a lack of innovation but the inability to scale successful ideas to reach millions of people across the continent.

Hamzat, who was speaking recently at the fifth edition of Texcellence in Lagos, said African countries must dismantle bureaucratic bottlenecks, establish predictable policies and implement institutional reforms that would enable technology-driven businesses to grow and deliver widespread economic and social benefits.

The event, themed ‘Accelerating Africa’s Digital Future Lacks Direction and a Sustained Force,’ brought together stakeholders to discuss strategies for strengthening the continent’s digital economy.

Texcellence is an annual tech summit attracting public and private sectors with technology experts. The fifth edition attracted international speakers from some African countries like Uganda, Kenya, South Africa among others.

Hamzat said governments must provide reliable infrastructure, predictable regulations and adequate funding to enable technology businesses to grow and deliver measurable benefits to citizens.

He outlined measures being taken by Lagos State to accelerate digital development and called for stronger collaboration between government and the private sector.

Hamzat stated: “Africa does not have an innovation problem. I will repeat that again. Africa does not have an innovation problem. We have a scaling problem. And it goes across all sectors.”

He cited CWG, a Nigerian technology company that began operations in Lagos in 1992, as an example of how businesses could grow in a supportive environment.

He said the company had expanded from a computer warehouse with six employees to a business listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), with subsidiaries in Ghana and Uganda and clients across Africa.

According to him, CWG’s growth demonstrated the importance of a large market and a stable business environment that rewarded excellence and encouraged long-term investment.

The deputy governor disclosed that Lagos had adopted a shared fibre-optic infrastructure model to reduce duplication of telecommunications facilities, with about 3,000 kilometres of fibre laid and plans for a unified 6,000-kilometre network backed by an additional $22million investment.

He added that more than seven million residents had enrolled in the state’s residents’ identity management system, while smart cameras installed along major roads were helping with traffic monitoring.

On improving the business environment, Hamzat said the state introduced an electronic physical planning permit system in April, allowing applicants to process and track permits online.

He said the initiative had reduced the steps required to obtain permits from 29 to seven without increasing statutory fees.

Hamzat also disclosed that the Lagos State Science, Research and Innovation Council had supported 18 researchers and more than 75 start-ups. He said the government was proposing legislation to dedicate a fixed portion of its annual budget to research, development and innovation.

The founder of CWG and Texcellence host, Austin Okere, noted that the desire to address poor customer service and unreliable technology delivery inspired him to establish the company, which has grown into a major player in Nigeria’s information technology industry.

He said he founded CWG after becoming dissatisfied with the failure of his former employer to meet delivery commitments to customers, warning that businesses risk losing their reputation when they fail to keep their promises.

He added that the company’s commitment to developing Nigeria’s technology industry informed the establishment of the CWG Academy, which trains professionals not only for the company but also for its customers and competitors.

According to him, the initiative was introduced partly in response to the departure of skilled Nigerian technology professionals to international companies entering the local market.

He explained that Texcellence was created to bring technology companies, governments, customers and other stakeholders together to discuss how Africa could strengthen its digital infrastructure and accelerate technological development.

While speaking with journalists, the Chief Operating Officer of CWG , Mr. Afolabi Sobande, advocated greater investment in indigenous technology development, stressing that Africa has the capacity to develop solutions to its challenges rather than depend continually on imported technologies.

He said the annual conference, which began in 2021, was established to stimulate conversations about Africa’s capacity to drive technological development and encourage stakeholders to explore solutions that could address the continent’s needs.

World.title: 2027: Tompolo Explains Why Oyo Should Stand with Tinubu
World.content:
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has called on the people of Oyo State to vote massively for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s reelection as one of their own.

He made the call as he donated 32 vehicles to the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Oyo State for grassroots mobilisation.

Speaking through his representative, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited, Chief Kestin Pondi, at the inauguration of the movement’s Oyo State structure held at the Liberty Stadium in Ibadan yesterday, Tompolo said the vehicles were donated to support the Movement’s campaign, which is aimed at mobilising votes for Tinubu’s re-election and the election of other candidates under the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The PBAT Door-to-Door Grand Patron reminded Oyo people that President Tinubu is their son and they should ensure that he returns to office to complete the two-term turn of the south.

Tompolo commended the president for the far-reaching reforms in critical sectors, saying that among other positives, the reforms have increased resources available to state governments to pay salaries, pensions and execute major projects.

He called on members of the Movement to take the message of the president’s reelection to all parts of the state, stressing that the people of Oyo State should be among those who give Tinubu another four years to consolidate his reforms.

“We are here today to tell you that we are coming to join you to canvass for votes across the country for your son, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. What Tompolo is preaching is that Tinubu is doing very well. Tinubu’s reform policies are fantastic. We want you to support President Tinubu’s reelection for him to continue with the good work he is doing,” he said.

Also speaking at the rally, the APC governorship candidate for Oyo State, Senator Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, stated that the Oyo APC put in all efforts to deliver the state.

According to him, Oyo State has stayed disconnected from the centre for too long.

Alli thanked Tompolo for his donation and for his support for President Tinubu. This is as he called on party members and his supporters to ensure that the vehicles donated by the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement are deployed across the state during the campaigns.

He said: “We are very grateful. I want to assure you that we are going to make judicious use of all these vehicles and all

other items that you may want to give us or from any other support group.

“As far as we are concerned in Oyo State, we have stayed out of the government for too long, and we are sincerely working assiduously to ensure that we take over the mantle of leadership in Oyo State,” he stated.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Mr. Sunday Asuku, called on the people of Oyo State, especially the youths, to firmly support Tinubu’s re-election.

Asuku described the president’s reforms as necessary for the country’s economic growth and sustained development. He further described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the people-oriented policies that has made a positive impact.

Asuku urged members of the Movement to take the campaign for President Tinubu’s second term to every nook and cranny of the state.

World.title: IsDB Group, Nigeria, Cameroon, Others Partner on Devt
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

The Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) has moved to strengthen the longstanding partnership between Nigeriaand the IsDB Group to advance cooperation under the IsDB Group Country Engagement Framework (CEF) 2026–2028. The bank disclosed that the move was also to support Nigeria’s development priorities, such as infrastructure, private sector development, Islamic finance, and economic diversification.

The action, according to a statement issued and made available to THISDAY by the IsDB Communication Director, Ahmed Abu Ghazeleh, was taken yesterday when Chairman of the IsDB Group, Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, held a productive bilateral meeting with the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy of the Federal.

Republic of Nigeria and IsDB Governor, Mr.

Taiwo Oyedele, on the margins of the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

Dr. Al Jasser expressed appreciation for Nigeria’s continued support for the IsDB Group, and commended the country’s efforts to diversify its economy and enhance competitiveness.

He reaffirmed the group’s commitment to supporting Nigeria’s development

agenda through the IsDB and its affiliated institutions: the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector (ICD), the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC), the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit (ICIEC), and the IsDB Institute (IsDBi).

The two parties reviewed the IsDB Group’s expanding portfolio in Nigeria, and also discussed progress in implementing the CEF, which aims to accelerate economic transformation through infrastructure development, inclusive human capital development, private sector growth, and the expansion of Islamic finance and the halal economy.

The meeting also highlighted the approval of six projects across priority sectors, including agriculture, renewable energy, health, infrastructure, and climate resilience.

“These projects are expected to make a significant contribution to sustainable growth, economic resilience, and improved livelihoods across the country.

“Building on the momentum from the IsDB Group Day held in Lagos earlier this year, the discussions reaffirmed Nigeria and the IsDB Group’s joint commitment to delivering impactful, large-scale development programmes aligned with the country’s long-term development

objectives and Agenda 2050,” the statement added.

Meanwhile, Al Jasser also met with the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Ms. Kristalina Georgieva, on the sidelines of the 2026 World Bank–IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok to discuss expanding cooperation in Islamic finance, financial stability, capacity development, and knowledge exchange.

The statement disclosed that the discussions reviewed progress under the IsDB–IMF cooperation framework, including joint initiatives in Islamic finance and the forthcoming joint report on Islamic banking and financial stability.

“The two leaders also explored opportunities to strengthen collaboration on regional economic analysis, macroeconomic developments, and financial stability, with particular attention to issues affecting IsDB Member Countries,” it added

According to the statement, Dr. Al Jasser emphasised the importance of scaling up joint capacity-development programmes through the IsDB Institute and the IMF Middle East Centre for Economics and Finance, building on the institutions’ recent cooperation in Islamic banking, financial regulation, and related policy areas.

The meeting reaffirmed IsDB and the IMF’s shared commitment to promoting practical cooperation through joint research, capacity development, policy dialogue, and knowledge-sharing initiatives that support resilient, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth.

IsDB and Cameroon Sign EUR 212.35 Million Financing Agreement for Major Transport Project.

Also, the statement noted that in Bangkok, Thailand, IsDB and the Republic of

Cameroon signed a EUR 212.35 million financing agreement to support the

Douala–Bafoussam Road Rehabilitation Project, a major transport initiative covering a critical corridor that connects the country’s Littoral and West regions.

The agreement, the statement said, was signed by the Chairman of the IsDB Group, Al Jasser, and Cameroon’s Minister of Economy, Planning and Regional Development and IsDB Governor, Mr. Alamine Ousmane Mey, on the sidelines of the annual meetings in Bangkok.

The project aims to enhance regional connectivity, lower transportation costs, facilitate the movement of goods to domestic and international markets through the Port of Douala, and expand access to economic opportunities for communities along the corridor. It includes rehabilitating 218 kilometres of national roads and 108 kilometres of feeder roads, and improving social infrastructure, including classrooms, health centres, water facilities, markets, and agricultural facilities.

After the signing ceremony, the two sides held bilateral discussions to explore ways to further strengthen cooperation to support the country’s development priorities.

Dr. Al Jasser commended the strong partnership between the IsDB Group and Cameroon, noting

that cumulative IsDB Group approvals for the country have surpassed the established target and that the active portfolio spans several sectors, including energy, transport, and agriculture.

He reaffirmed the IsDB Group’s commitment to supporting Cameroon’s sustainable and inclusive

development agenda.

The bank chief emphasised the need to accelerate project implementation to maximise development impact and ensure timely delivery of approved investments.

The discussions also reviewed progress in preparing Cameroon’s upcoming Country Engagement.

Framework (2027–2030), which is expected to guide future cooperation in priority sectors, including agriculture, energy, water, transport, education, and health.

Since Cameroon joined the IsDB in 1977, the IsDB Group has approved US$4.22 billion in financing for the country, reflecting nearly five decades of development cooperation.

Also, the IsDB and Benin Republic strengthened the development partnership by signing €326 million in financing agreements.

Al Jasser and the Benin Republic Delegate Minister to the Minister of Economy and

Finance, in charge of External Resource Mobilisation and Debt Management,

Mr. Hugues Oscar Lokossou, disclosed this at a bilateral meeting in Bangkok, which

provided the opportunity to discuss Benin’s development priorities and explore

avenues for further cooperation, particularly in infrastructure, agriculture, and other sectors.

Following the meeting, IsDB and the Republic of Benin signed co-financing agreements for two key development projects, which included the Godomey–Ouidah–Hillacondji Road Capacity Expansion and Upgrading Project, with a total cost of €576.06 million, and will receive €306.89 million in IsDB financing to improve road safety and

efficiency, reduce travel times and transport costs, and strengthen regional connectivity and trade

along the Abidjan–Lagos corridor.

“The Sustainable Intensification of Legume-Based Systems for Soil Fertility, Agricultural Resilience, and Food Security Project, with a total cost of €20.70 million, will receive €19.17 million in IsDB financing to promote sustainable legume-based agriculture, improve soil fertility, strengthen food

security, and enhance climate resilience across five development poles,” the statement added.

Al Jasser, according to the statement, reaffirmed the IsDB Group’s commitment to its longstanding partnership with

the Republic of Benin, emphasizing the importance of continued collaboration to advance sustainable development and deliver tangible benefits to communities.

World.title: Former NPA Boss Dabo, Resigns as APC Chairman, Dumps Party
World.content:
Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

The Caucus Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Dambatta Local Government Area of Kano State, Aminu Dabo, has resigned from the ruling party.

Dabo, a former Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), resigned as both caucus chairman and as a member of the party with immediate effect.

According to a press statement signed by his media and publicity aide, Audu Usman, Dabo is yet to announce his next political move.

In his resignation letter dated October 7, 2026, and addressed to the APC Chairman of Dambatta Gabas Ward, Dambatta Local Government, Dabo said the decision followed “careful consideration of my personal reasons and future endeavours.”

“I remain grateful for the cordial relationship I enjoyed and appreciative of the experience gained during my time of service,” he said, thanking the party leadership for the opportunity and confidence reposed in him.

“I sincerely appreciate the support and opportunity I have received from the party leadership,” the letter added.

World.title: MPB Calls for Unity Among Veterans as Pensioners Protest in Abuja
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chairman of the Military Pensions Board (MPB), Air Vice Marshal Mikail Abdulraheem, has urged military veterans to unite under a common platform to strengthen their advocacy for improved pensions and welfare.

Abdulraheem made the call at a press conference following a meeting with protesting military pensioners in Abuja.

He explained that the board was bound by the legal framework governing military pension administration and could not act outside its provisions. He advised pensioners seeking changes to existing legislation to approach the National Assembly.

The chairman also urged veterans to overcome divisions within their ranks, noting that a united association would be better positioned to influence government policies on pensions and other welfare matters.

“Veterans should form a very strong, cohesive body that can speak with one voice,” he said, adding that political leaders and presidential aspirants should give due consideration to their concerns, particularly during election periods.

Abdulraheem further appealed to journalists to verify allegations concerning the board before publication, warning that unsubstantiated reports could undermine public confidence in the institution and jeopardise the interests of military retirees.

“Whenever you hear something negative about the board, please do not be in a hurry to publish. Verify it with the board, and we are ready to speak to you,” he said.

He stressed that responsible reporting was essential to protecting the board’s credibility and the pension interests of serving personnel who would eventually retire.

“I want you to understand that I am a son of a veteran. I will become a veteran myself in the future. If I cheat veterans today, I will also be affecting myself because I will eventually belong to the same community. It is therefore not in my interest to deny anyone what is legitimately due to them. However, we must be guided by the law.

“There are situations where people may have strong feelings about an issue, but the law provides the procedure that must be followed. I appeal to everyone to approach this matter with an open mind. Let us discuss the specific issues raised in the letter before moving on to other matters.

“The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission was also invited to provide clarification so that the relevant calculations and applicable provisions could be examined transparently. The board is guided by the relevant pension legislation, including the applicable provisions of the Pension Reform Act. We want the issues to be discussed openly and resolved based on the facts and the law,” he said.

A military veteran, Master Warrant Officer Sadura Augustine, said the pensioners had visited the board’s headquarters to discuss issues affecting military retirees and seek clarification on their pensions.

“The issue before us concerns the consequential adjustment and the amounts received by pensioners. We believe in transparency and access to information. The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission has a salary structure relevant to pension computation, and we want to understand how it was applied in our case.

“Our concern is that the announced percentages do not appear to correspond with the increases received by some pensioners. We want to understand our gross pension entitlements and how the adjustments were calculated to arrive at the amounts we are now receiving,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu/Shettima PCC: Nigeria Must Sustain Economic Reform
World.content:
Aminat Hassan in Abuja

One of the spoke persons of the Tinubu/Shettima Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) 2027, Segun Showunmi, has urged Nigerians to sustain President Bola Ahmed Tinubu-led administration’s economic reform programme and consolidate what he described as the foundations of national renewal.

Showunmi, in an interactive session with journalists in Abuja yesterday argued that the country was at a defining moment in its development and needed continuity of policy direction, stronger institutions and accelerated implementation of reforms to achieve sustainable economic growth.

He said the 2027 presidential election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to decide whether to continue with the current administration’s development agenda, expressing the conviction that a second term for Tinubu would offer an opportunity to deepen ongoing reforms and translate their expected benefits into improved living standards.

“My position is clear: I support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a second term because I believe Nigeria must keep moving forward,” Showunmi stated.

He maintained that the Nigerian project transcended individual politicians, political parties and electoral contests, describing the country’s long-term development as a collective responsibility requiring national unity, sustained investment and consistency of purpose.

According to him, Nigeria must not abandon its pursuit of prosperity but should consolidate ongoing efforts to build a more productive, stable and competitive economy.

Showunmi acknowledged that Nigeria had long faced structural economic challenges, including inadequate infrastructure, limited productivity and difficulties in converting its human and natural resources into broadly shared prosperity.

However, he expressed optimism that the country could overcome these constraints through sustained economic reforms, increased investment and stronger productive capacity.

He said the Tinubu administration had embarked on reforms intended to reposition the economy, address longstanding distortions, strengthen public finances and create conditions for sustainable growth.

The political advocate argued that the value of the reforms should ultimately be measured by their capacity to stimulate investment, generate employment, improve infrastructure, strengthen businesses and enhance the government’s ability to provide essential services.

“We are not simply trying to manage an economy. We are building the foundations of a nation that can compete, produce, innovate and prosper,” he said.

Showunmi maintained that countries which achieved lasting prosperity did so by sustaining their development ambitions, strengthening institutions and providing the policy stability required for productive investment to flourish.

He urged Nigerians to look beyond immediate political considerations and focus on the country’s development prospects over the next decade and beyond, including industrial expansion, infrastructure delivery, skills development and improved opportunities for businesses.

Explaining his support for Tinubu’s re-election, Showunmi identified leadership, policy direction, institutional capacity and the ability to mobilise citizens around a common national objective as important considerations in determining the country’s future.

He said the administration’s focus on economic restructuring, infrastructure, education, energy reform, investment mobilisation and public-sector institutions represented important areas of national development.

According to him, continuity in government would provide an opportunity to build on existing initiatives, strengthen implementation and accelerate progress towards the country’s economic objectives.

He nevertheless emphasised that the next phase of governance should place greater attention on delivering tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians.

“A second term should be a period of accelerated delivery, expanded opportunity and a more visible connection between national economic progress and household prosperity,” he stated.

Showunmi said Nigerians should expect the next phase of the administration’s agenda to produce stronger investment, increased domestic production, improved infrastructure, expanded opportunities for young people and a wider distribution of economic benefits.

Highlighting initiatives undertaken by the Tinubu administration since May 2023, Showunmi pointed to developments across education, electricity, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, taxation and public administration.

He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund as an additional avenue for eligible students to finance tertiary education, describing access to education as an important component of the country’s long-term human-capital development.

He said Nigeria’s young population represented a strategic national asset that required investment in knowledge, technical skills, digital capabilities and entrepreneurial development.

On electricity, he referenced the Electricity Act 2023, which provides a framework for states to develop electricity markets within the applicable legal and regulatory arrangements.

According to him, greater participation and investment in the electricity sector could create opportunities for locally responsive energy solutions and improved power supply.

Showunmi also identified major road projects, including the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Super Highway and Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano highway, as examples of the administration’s infrastructure ambitions.

He said transportation infrastructure remained essential to integrating the national economy, connecting communities to markets and lowering the cost of moving goods and services.

In agriculture, he called for a more commercially productive sector capable of feeding the population, supporting agro-industries and generating export earnings.

He also advocated improved access to essential healthcare services and a coherent public-finance and taxation framework capable of supporting infrastructure development while maintaining a competitive environment for businesses.

With the 2027 presidential election approaching, Showunmi urged Nigerians to support Tinubu for a second term, describing the choice as an opportunity to consolidate economic reforms and accelerate the country’s development agenda.

He said his position was based on the belief that continued policy direction would allow the government to build on initiatives already underway and pursue more ambitious economic and social outcomes.

He identified increased investment, industrial development, improved infrastructure, expanded youth opportunities, stronger communities and more widely shared prosperity as priorities for the next phase of governance.

Showunmi also called for a closer connection between national economic performance and improvements in household welfare, arguing that the benefits of development should be felt more directly by citizens.

He said the next phase of the administration should focus on translating national ambitions into practical outcomes that Nigerians could see and experience in their daily lives.

“My support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is an expression of this conviction. I believe his administration’s reform programme offers Nigeria an important opportunity to consolidate its economic foundations and accelerate the pursuit of inclusive prosperity,” he stated.

He urged citizens, entrepreneurs, workers, farmers and young people to contribute to the national development process through enterprise, investment, innovation and collective commitment to national progress.

World.title: Is El Niño behind the heatwave gripping three SA provinces?
World.content:
A blazing sun shines over a city as heatwave conditions persist in parts of South Africa. Image: Unsplash

El Niño has contributed to the heatwaves affecting KwaZulu-Natal, the Eastern Cape and Mpumalanga, according to the South African Weather Service (SAWS).

The weather service has warned that persistently high temperatures will continue in parts of the three provinces.

Heatwave conditions will persist until early next week.



El Niño contributes to rising temperatures

According to EyeWitnessNews, SAWS forecaster Andre Fourie said the El Niño weather phenomenon has played a role in the current heatwave conditions.

“The heatwave does have something to do with the El Niño; it is indicating that it’s already in it strong state so therefore, we were expecting this above normal temperatures going into summer. El Niño would possibly contribute to those higher temperatures that are resulting in the heatwave conditions.”

Fourie also urged residents in affected provinces to take extra precautions to stay cool during the heatwave.

How long will the heatwaves last?

According to SAWS, the heatwave advisories are expected to remain in place until different dates across the three provinces.

Parts of the Chris Hani, OR Tambo and Alfred Nzo district municipalities in the Eastern Cape will experience persistently high temperatures until Saturday, 17 October.

Northern KwaZulu-Natal could experience heatwave conditions until Sunday, 18 October.



Meanwhile, parts of Mpumalanga, excluding areas along the Escarpment, face persistently high temperatures until Monday, 19 October.

How to stay safe during the heatwave

Residents should drink enough water, avoid prolonged exposure to the sun and limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest part of the day.

Children, older people and those with existing health conditions may face a greater risk of heat-related illness.

SAWS has urged residents to follow the latest weather updates and take precautions while high temperatures persist.

World.title: Where is former Kaizer Chiefs striker Bernard Parker now
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs striker Bernard Parker has been making headlines in recent weeks following developments in both his professional and personal life.

The retired forward recently parted ways with TS Galaxy after a brief spell as head coach, while also announcing his separation from his wife, Kacha Stephanovic.

Parker, affectionately known as Die Hond, enjoyed a successful playing career before transitioning into coaching following his retirement.



Parker first rose to prominence at Benoni Premier United before earning a move overseas following his impressive performances for Bafana Bafana at the 2009 FIFA Confederations Cup.

He subsequently joined Kaizer Chiefs, where he spent a decade and established himself as one of the club’s most recognisable players.

During his time at Naturena, the former striker won four trophies with Amakhosi.



In 2022, Parker left Chiefs and joined TS Galaxy, where he spent two seasons before bringing his playing career to an end.

He subsequently moved into coaching at the Mpumalanga-based club, initially working with the reserve team before being promoted to head coach towards the end of the 2025/26 season.

Parker guided Galaxy to the Nedbank Cup final, but his team ultimately lost to Durban City.



Why did Bernard Parker leave TS Galaxy?

Parker’s time as head coach proved short-lived. TS Galaxy CEO Tim Sukazi recently confirmed that the former striker had left the club after being removed from the head coach position.

Parker was reportedly offered an opportunity to serve as an assistant coach in the club’s DStv Diski Challenge team, but he did not accept the role.

His departure has raised questions about what comes next for the former Chiefs star, who had only recently begun his journey as a senior coach.



Parker’s departure from TS Galaxy coincided with the announcement that he and his wife, Kacha Stephanovic, were separating.

In his statement, the former footballer apologised for disappointing and hurting his wife, while acknowledging that he was dealing with personal struggles.

The announcement sparked widespread discussion on social media, with some users questioning aspects of the couple’s relationship.



On Thursday, the former Bafana Bafana international issued a statement calling for privacy as he navigates this period of change.

As things stand, Bernard Parker has left TS Galaxy and is no longer serving as the club’s head coach. He also declined the reported offer to join the DDC technical team as an assistant coach.

His next move in football remains unclear, with no new coaching appointment confirmed in the information available.



For now, Parker appears focused on addressing the circumstances surrounding his departure from the club and his personal life. He has urged the public to respect his privacy as he deals with these developments.

What do you think of Parker’s situation?

World.title: Matric exams begin: Department reports on NSC start
World.content:
The Department of Basic Education announced that there was a positive start to the 2026 National Senior Certificate (NSC) exams, which officially started on Tuesday 13 October.

MATRIC FINAL EXAMS 2026 OFF TO ‘POSITIVE’ START

The Department of Basic Education (DBE) said that there was a smooth start to the NSC exams, as candidates across all nine provinces sat for Computer Applications Technology (CAT) Paper 1 Practical and various language papers on Tuesday 13 October.

A record 962,832 candidates registered are registered for the NSC 2026 exams. 815 051 are full-time and 147 781 part-time candidates. The exams run until 26 November.



The Department of Basic Education (DBE) warned that cheating in any form will not be tolerated. Minister Siviwe Gwarube described the department’s approach as zero-tolerance.Gwarube also said candidate and parent pledge agreements have been introduced to promote integrity, alongside a 24-hour hotline for reporting suspected irregularities.

“The commencement of the 2026 National Senior Certificate examinations is an important moment for our learners and the basic education sector. Every examination represents an opportunity for learners to demonstrate the knowledge and skills they have acquired over the years. We encourage the Class of 2026 to approach each paper with confidence, remain focused and give their very best. As a nation, we have a collective responsibility to support our learners as they take this important step towards their futures,” said Minister Gwarube.

Know your timetable. Mark down the dates of each of your papers and keep checking for any updates.

Leave your phones behind. No cellphones will be allowed into exam venues.

Leave your notes behind.

Use free revision sources, such as past papers and study guides.

Take a look at what happens if a learner is sick during the NSC exams here.

World.title: Cape Town braces for rain as thousands head to weekend events
World.content:
Cloudy skies over Cape Town as the city prepares for a busy weekend of events. Image: AI illustration

Cape Town is preparing for a busy weekend, with around 100 000 people expected to attend events across the city as rain threatens to disrupt outdoor plans.

The City of Cape Town has approved 20 events from Friday to Sunday including rugby, football and a major marathon.

What does the weather forecast say?

The latest forecast points to a cool and wet weekend, with Saturday temperatures expected to reach 17 degrees Celsius.



Rain is more likely during Saturday morning, followed by cloudy conditions in the afternoon.

Sunday could bring further showers, with temperatures reaching around 16 degrees Celsius.

Although the forecast suggests rain, conditions may change throughout the weekend.



Cape Town could experience a cool and wet weekend, with a 60% chance of rain and 3mm of rainfall forecast.

The DHL Stormers will face Bristol Bears at DHL Stadium on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 16:15.

Meanwhile, Athlone Stadium will host the SAFA Cape Town Coca-Cola Amateur Cup finals, with matches starting at 13:00.



Around 30 000 runners are expected to take part in the inaugural Nelson Mandela Marathon on Sunday.

The event includes 42km, 21km, 10km and 5km races, with routes passing through several parts of Cape Town.

Morning showers could affect runners, particularly those taking part in the earlier races.



Road closures expected

The City has warned motorists to expect road closures and traffic disruptions around several event venues.

Road restrictions will affect parts of the DHL Stadium precinct on Saturday, while Sunday’s marathon will disrupt traffic along sections of the city centre, Green Point and Milnerton.

Motorists should allow extra travelling time, check road closures and consider public transport where possible.



Residents and visitors should also follow the latest weather updates before heading outdoors.

World.title: The Klein Karoo towns where drugs are taking over
World.content:
South Africa’s small towns have an unforgettable warmth and charm.

But in multiple Klein Karoo towns, the scourge of drugs has taken over, deteriorating that welcoming essence.

The rise in drugs also means a rise in crime.



Drugs ruin the charm of South Africa’s small towns

Crime in Dysselsdorp, a predominantly Afrikaans town nestled in the Kammanassie mountains, peaked in 2025.

The town recorded the most crimes since the South African Police Service (SAPS) started publishing statistics in 2013.

Dysselsdorp is a farming community of 18 839 people, stretching 351 square kilometres.

Between Outdshoorn and De Rust, the town’s slower pace is slowly being overtaken by drugs.

In the year ending March 2026, Dysselsdorp recorded 124 more drug-related crimes than the year before.

Drug-related crimes were also the most reported crime in the area. They were reported 3 times as often as common assault, which took second place.



Naturally, as drug-related crime spiked, so did many other crimes.

Residential and business burglary, theft, and assault all increased.

In the first quarter (April to June 2026), things have not improved.

Instead, the crime data suggests Dysselsdorp could be on track for a record-breaking year.

Crime is up 28.1% in the first quarter of 2026, compared to the first quarter of 2025.

Drug-related crime is up 65.8% in the first quarter, and again it takes the top spot as the most reported crime in Dysselsdorp.

Now it is nearly four times as high as theft, the next most frequently reported crime.

Drugs Spreading Across the Klein Karoo

In neighbouring De Rust, things are not any better.

In one year, drug-related crime increased 190% in the area. Residential burglary, stock theft, and business burglary also increased.

In the first quarter, drug crimes nearly doubled.

In Ladismith, a tourism hotspot in the Klein Karoo, drug crime is up 12.9% in the first quarter.

Uniondale and Calitzdorp have also encountered a rise in drug-related crime.

Drug Trail to the Klein Karoo

This region has no major airports or ports.

The Klein Karoo isn’t on any major drug trafficking routes.

Therefore, the region should be, by all intents and purposes, sheltered from the kind of drug-related crime that has overtaken parts of Cape Town and the Cape Winelands.

But drugs enter these small and rural towns through two methods:

Home-based manufacturing of drugs like crystal meth (Tik) and a heroin and dagga mix (Nyaope/Whoonga).

Drug networks seeking safety from drug enforcement on major trafficking routes by setting up shop in smaller towns to avoid detection.

Dysselsdorp is 24 kilometres from Oudtshoorn and about a 90-minute drive from the small Mossel Bay harbour that is developing into a drug-trafficking route.

World.title: GBV panic alerts: More than one a day, and most involve domestic abuse
World.content:
People facing gender-based violence are using emergency panic alerts to call for help. Image: Pexels, for illustrative purposes

GBV panic alerts are revealing a hidden side of South Africa’s gender-based violence crisis.

Some people in danger are reaching for a panic button meant for car breakdowns.

And the data shows just how often it’s happening.



Most of the alerts involved domestic abuse.

Between 14 July and 1 October 2026, the Automobile Association of South Africa’s emergency response service received 88 panic alerts tagged as gender-based or sexual violence.

That’s more than one a day.

WHAT THE GBV PANIC ALERTS SHOW

The alerts came through a private emergency network designed mainly for motorists and roadside breakdowns.

The service tagged the 88 alerts as follows:

Domestic abuse: 61

61 Gender-based violence: 14

14 Rape: 12

12 Sexual offences: 4

4 Stalking: 1

Some alerts carried more than one tag.



With 61 of the 88 alerts tagged as domestic abuse, most involved violence at home, which usually comes from a partner or family member.

A CRISIS THAT HASN’T LET UP

The alerts come during a period of intense public concern about gender-based violence (GBV).

By 5 October, the number of women killed in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, since July had reached 12.

Between April and June 2026, police recorded 569 women murdered and another 1,052 women who survived attempted murder.

One in three women in South Africa will experience physical or sexual violence during her lifetime, according to the Centre for Applied Legal Studies at Wits University.

WHAT THE GOVERNMENT IS DOING

On Tuesday, 29 September, President Cyril Ramaphosa announced new measures to tackle violence against women, following the Ekurhuleni killings.

He ordered police and the National Prosecuting Authority to review unresolved murder, attempted murder, rape and other GBV cases within 90 days.

He said the reviews would be followed by funded plans to tackle hotspots and case backlogs.

“This cannot be accepted as a normal part of life in South Africa,” Ramaphosa said.

WHY THE DATA MATTERS

Private panic alerts only capture a small part of the picture.

Many survivors never report abuse at all.

But the figures show that people in danger are reaching for whatever help is closest, even when that help exists for a different purpose.

WHERE TO GET HELP

If you or someone you know is experiencing abuse, call the GBV Command Centre on 0800 428 428, available 24/7. You can also dial *120*7867# from any cellphone, free of charge.

In an emergency, contact the South African Police Service (SAPS) on 10111, or dial 112 from any cellphone.
