World.title: Government calls for restoration of ecosystems
World.content:
Government has called for community involvement in the protection and restoration of critical ecosystems.

‎Isoka District Administrative Officer, Sarah Sooli says all environmental conservation efforts must take into account the livelihood needs of people who depend on the same natural resources for survival.

‎Ms Sooli notes that local communities should be involved in identifying environmental challenges and developing practical solutions, stating that their participation is essential to the success and sustainability of conservation initiatives.

‎The District Administrative Officer said this during the Global Environment Facility (GEF-9) Scoping Mission for Muchinga Province, held at Isoka Town Council Chamber.

‎The meeting was aimed at developing a funding proposal for the restoration and protection of critical ecosystems within the Upper Luangwa catchment.

‎Ms Sooli said stakeholders need to understand the circumstances that drive communities into activities that contribute to environmental degradation and work together to identify sustainable alternatives.

‎She cited charcoal production as an example of an activity that, despite putting pressure on forests, provided an income for some households.

‎“We need to work closely with our communities and understand the challenges they face. If people depend on activities such as charcoal burning to support their families, we must explore sustainable alternatives that protect the environment while also addressing their livelihood needs,” she said.

‎Ms Sooli said government departments, traditional leaders and other stakeholders should collaborate in promoting environmental awareness and supporting communities to adopt practices that would protect natural resources without undermining their livelihoods.

‎Meanwhile, GEF-9 Scoping Mission Consultant, Royd Vinya, said agricultural expansion, infrastructure development, population growth and the production of charcoal and timber were among the major drivers of environmental degradation in Muchinga Province.

‎Professor Vinya said the increasing demand for agricultural land was contributing to forest loss, soil erosion and habitat destruction, while agricultural chemicals are finding their way into water systems and negatively affecting aquatic life.

‎He said Isoka’s agricultural activities need to be managed sustainably to prevent continued forest clearance and damage to surrounding ecosystems.

‎“People must survive. The charcoal producers have responded by producing charcoal because they must feed their children. We must understand that they are also trying to make a living,” Professor Vinya said.

‎He said the proposed intervention should therefore address the underlying causes of environmental degradation by promoting sustainable land management, restoring degraded areas and conserving biodiversity.

‎Professor Vinya explained that the Upper Luangwa catchment was an important biodiversity area supporting various plant and animal species, wetlands and other critical ecosystems, but continued pressure from human activities threatened its long-term sustainability.

‎He said the proposed project would focus on biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management and restoration, as well as reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

‎Professor Vinya added that the ultimate goal was to ensure communities could continue benefiting from natural resources while maintaining the ecological systems that support agriculture, water resources and other livelihoods.

‎And Ministry of Green Economy and Environment Senior Environmental Management Officer, Mirriam Mbewe, said Zambia is eligible to access funding from the Global Environment Facility because the country was part of several international environmental agreements supported by the facility.

‎Ms Mbewe, who represented the GEFs Operational Focal Point person said the facility provided financial support to developing countries to address global environmental challenges, including biodiversity loss, land degradation and climate change.

‎She said the funding framework also supported initiatives in chemicals and waste management, international waters and integrated programmes that linked environmental protection with sustainable livelihoods.

‎Ms Mbewe said the scoping mission was an important step towards identifying environmental priorities and shaping a funding proposal that aligned local needs with the GEF’s strategic areas of support.

‎She added that Zambia had implemented 30 regional, sub-regional and global projects since the facility was established, demonstrating the country’s engagement with GEF-supported environmental initiatives.

World.title: North-Western holds 16 Days of Activism against GBV preparatory meeting
World.content:
North-Western Province Senior Gender Officer in Charge of Gender Rights Protection, Leah Chivube, has commended the steady increase in the number of boys and men reporting Gender-Based Violence (GBV) cases in the country.

In an interview with ZANIS News today following the first preparatory meeting for the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, Ms Chivube said deliberate activities have been lined up to raise awareness of GBV among men.

Ms Chivube said the activities will be held ahead of the official launch and will include the commemoration of International Men’s Day on November 19.

“We have lined up activities prior to the actual launch, which include the commemoration of International Men’s Day on the 19th of November,” Ms Chivube said.

She said police statistics on the number of men reporting GBV cases showed that more men could come forward if they were provided with the right information and a safe environment in which to report their experiences.

“As a committee, we will have sporting activities such as soccer, chess and a match to commemorate International Men’s Day because we want to honour and appreciate their efforts,” Ms Chivube said.

She said the activities would also encourage men to report any form of GBV they might be experiencing.

Meanwhile, Ms Chivube disclosed that the committee planned to host a fundraising event, with proceeds going towards supporting GBV survivors.

She said the provincial theme for the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence was “Unite to End Gender-Based Violence, Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity,” which had been derived from the international theme.

World.title: Women cooperatives urged to venture in value addition
World.content:
Chilanga Acting District Commissioner, Maureen Chilende, has urged women cooperatives to venture into value addition in order to grow their agricultural enterprise projects.

Ms Chilende says the agricultural sector has huge potential to contribute to the economic development of the country through value addition and access to markets.

She said this when she officiated at the Agape Women’s Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society 25 years Silver Jubilee celebration held in Chilanga today.

Ms Chilende has noted that value addition will enable cooperatives to earn more income, extend shelf life of their products and compete favorably on both local and regional markets.

“I urge the community to support locally produced products. When we buy local merchandise, we support local businesses, create opportunities and contribute to community development,” said Ms Chilende.

She has further encouraged the Women’s Cooperative to practice transparency and accountability and maintain proper records and invest in sustainable income generating activities.

Ms Chilende has observed that good governance within cooperatives is key to attracting partnerships and growing their businesses.

“I therefore encourage Agape Women’s Multi-Purpose Cooperative to continue building partnerships that can strengthen its business operations and expand its impact,” she said.

And Chilanga District Small and Medium Enterprises Development Officer, Eugene Maliwa, has urged cooperatives to generate income from various businesses and run their cooperatives without waiting for government grants.

Mr Maliwa has reaffirmed Government’s commitment to guide and support local cooperatives in growing their businesses.

He has indicated that cooperatives that diversify their income sources and embrace entrepreneurship are more resilient and sustainable in the long term.

World.title: ZRA calls for stronger international cooperation in tax administration
World.content:
Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) Commissioner General, Dingani Banda, has called for stronger international cooperation among tax administrations to address increasingly complex transactions, rising taxpayer expectations and other emerging challenges in revenue collection.

In a speech read on his behalf by Acting ZRA Commissioner General, Ernest Sigande, at a reception hosted by the British High Commission in Zambia, Rebecca Terzeon, for participants in the Commonwealth Association of Tax Administrators (CATA) Senior Leadership Programme, the commissioner said partnerships were essential to strengthening tax administration.

“Addressing these challenges requires not only strong institutions, but also cooperation, trust and a willingness to learn from one another,” Mr Banda said.

The remarks were made as Zambia hosts the first phase of the 2026/2027 Commonwealth Association of Tax Administrators (CATA) Senior Leadership Programme, which has brought together 28 delegates representing 20 tax administrations across 20 countries.

The Commissioner General said the programme provided an opportunity for tax officials from different jurisdictions to exchange experiences and strengthen professional relationships to support improved tax administration.

Mr Banda also highlighted the longstanding cooperation between Zambia, the United Kingdom and CATA, noting that continued support and shared learning in tax administration and capacity development had strengthened institutions and enhanced their ability to deliver on their mandates.

He urged participants to use the programme to build relationships and share experiences that would continue to benefit their respective tax administrations beyond the training period.

The Commissioner General thanked the British High Commissioner for hosting the reception and reaffirmed the importance of sustained collaboration in strengthening tax administration across participating countries.

Speaking earlier, British High Commissioner, Rebecca Terzeon, stressed the importance of a fair and predictable tax system in ensuring businesses contribute to national resources and economic growth benefits communities across Zambia.

The High Commissioner said effective taxation and the equitable distribution of public resources were essential to ensuring that economic growth translated into job creation and support for vulnerable members of society.

“Companies to be paying taxes that are fair and predictable so that they are contributing to the resources of the country,” the High Commissioner said.

Ms Terzeon said effective economic management required not only businesses to meet their tax obligations but also the fair distribution of resources to ensure communities benefited from economic progress.

She said economic growth should create employment opportunities and improve support for vulnerable people.

Ms Terzeon encouraged participants to use the programme to build lasting professional relationships, saying the networks and friendships developed during leadership training could prove valuable long after the course ended.

The High Commissioner said such connections could enable participants to seek advice and support from one another when confronted with professional challenges or new opportunities.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 16, 2026
World.content:
UK Threatens Visa Ban on Eritreans Over Deportation Dispute

UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has threatened to ban all Eritrean nationals from entering the UK unless the East African country agrees to accept more of its citizens facing deportation, including foreign national offenders. Initial measures, which took effect, restrict Eritrean diplomats from travelling more than 60km outside London without permission. The UK will also stop fast-track visas for VIPs. Eritrea has condemned the move as a political gimmick, accusing the UK of failing to engage in meaningful dialogue and disputing claims about cooperation on returns. The UK government maintains that Eritrea withdrew its cooperation earlier this year. However, migration experts have questioned whether the restrictions will be effective. They said that many Eritrean asylum seekers qualify for protection because of repression and forced military conscription in their home country.

DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Response Progresses in Bunia





Efforts to contain the Democratic Republic of Congo's worst-ever Ebola outbreak are showing progress in Bunia, Ituri province, where health workers are intensifying community awareness campaigns and home visits to encourage residents to seek medical care. The outbreak has reportedly killed more than 4,000 people in five months. It was declared a public health emergency of international concern by the World Health Organization. Fear of infection and misinformation have disrupted healthcare services, particularly maternity care, with maternal deaths in Bunia rising from an average of three to almost five a week, according to health officials. UNICEF has established 12 nurseries linked to health facilities to care for children separated from parents receiving Ebola treatment. Survivors are helping support vulnerable children. Despite improvements in community trust and healthcare attendance, the outbreak continues in other areas, where armed-group activity and insufficient humanitarian funding are hampering response efforts.

China Outlines Four Principles to Resolve Conflicts Across Africa

Chinese President Xi Jinping has outlined four principles for resolving conflicts in Africa. He has called for African-led solutions, respect for national sovereignty, an end to hostilities and efforts to address the root causes of insecurity. Speaking during a meeting with Togo's President of the Council of Ministers, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, in Beijing on October 13, Xi said African people should remain central to decisions affecting the continent. He urged parties involved in conflict resolution to respect the United Nations Charter, pursue dialogue and compromise, and combine immediate security measures with long-term development planning. His remarks come as several African regions, including Sudan, the Great Lakes region and the Horn of Africa, continue to face conflict and security challenges. The two leaders also agreed to strengthen China-Togo relations through cooperation in trade, infrastructure, renewable energy, digital technology and industrialisation. Xi encouraged Togo to take advantage of China's zero-tariff arrangements for African products.

Kenya Reflects on Raila Odinga Legacy One Year After His Death

One year after former Kenyan Prime Minister Raila Odinga's death, his legacy continues to shape debates about democracy, constitutional reform and the future of opposition politics. Odinga spent decades campaigning for multiparty democracy and played a significant role in Kenya's political reforms, including the adoption of the 2010 Constitution. His supporters credit him with promoting reconciliation and institutional change. His political alliances with former foes, critics said, diluted the opposition's ability to hold the government to account. His Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) party's future has also been in the spotlight, with party leaders warning it is in danger of losing its identity and support among ordinary Kenyans. His daughter Winnie Odinga has declared interest in the Nairobi Senate seat in the upcoming 2027 polls. As younger generations reflect on his contribution, questions remain over whether Kenya's political institutions and opposition parties will uphold the democratic principles associated with his legacy.

Nigerian Gospel Singer Toluwanisings Dies at 41

Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has died at the age of 41. In a statement shared on his Instagram account, the family asked fans to remember his wife, children and relatives in their prayers. Toluwanisings was known for his powerful vocals and energetic praise performances, with popular songs including Unreserved Praise, A Very Big God, Onibuore, E Lagbara and Owo Re Meji Meji. News of his death prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans, fellow musicians and public figures, including lawyer Pelumi Olajengbesi and comedian Woli Agba, who had previously called for prayers for the singer. His death comes months after he was involved in a road accident alongside members of his band. The family said funeral arrangements would be announced in due course.

World.title: South Africa: City Power Seeks Army Help Against Copper Thieves - South African News Briefs - October 16, 2026
World.content:
press review

City Power Seeks Army Help to Combat Copper Theft

Johannesburg City Power has asked the Defence Ministry to deploy the army to help combat copper theft and vandalism at its infrastructure, following repeated fires at the Central Substation in Marshalltown, reports EWN. The damage has destroyed millions of rands worth of equipment and left residents without electricity for weeks. City Power is replacing damaged equipment and installing new cables, but fears thieves will return. The utility is also seeking police assistance with tunnel inspections and stricter regulation of precious metal sales.

Alleged Pastor and Co-Accused Back in Court Over Baby’s Death



Self-proclaimed pastor Caiphus Mkhawane and his co-accused, Ntsako Mathebula and Amanda Mnguni, are set to appear in the Atteridgeville Magistrates' Court in Pretoria in connection with the death of a four-month-old baby, reports SABC News. The trio face charges including conspiracy to commit murder and fraud. Mkhawane faces additional allegations of rape, human trafficking, kidnapping and premeditated murder. The case was postponed for legal aid representation and bail investigations. The National Prosecuting Authority said it remains committed to holding perpetrators of gender-based violence accountable.

Fadiel Adams Case Set for Pretrial Conference

National Coloured Congress MP Fadiel Adams is set to appear in the Pinetown Magistrates' Court in Durban for a pretrial conference in his case involving three counts of fraud and two counts of defeating the ends of justice, reports EWN. Adams is accused of visiting two awaiting-trial inmates at Westville Prison in November 2024 and January 2025 and conducting audio-recorded interviews without authorisation. The inmates have since been convicted of separate murders. Prosecutors allege the visits may have interfered with police work, but Adams maintains he did nothing wrong.

World.title: Malawi: Gold Rush or Gold Bust? Malawi's Smuggling Crackdown Faces Credibility Test
World.content:
Malawi's latest bid to turn gold into a lifeline for its struggling economy is facing uncomfortable questions about the evidence on which it has been built.

A state-backed scheme designed to intercept gold before it is smuggled out of the country rests on a headline-grabbing claim that $100 million worth of the precious metal is lost annually through illegal trade. Yet, according to an analysis by Collins Mtika for the Mail & Guardian and the Centre for Investigative Journalism Malawi, the figure has never been publicly explained.

The programme, spearheaded by the Malawi Mining Investment Company (Mamico), aims to buy gold from artisanal miners operating at roughly 100 sites nationwide, funnel it through buying centres in Lilongwe, Kasungu and Nkhotakota, and ultimately sell it to the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM).

But a closer examination of the numbers reveals a troubling inconsistency.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Earlier this year, Mamico reported findings from a month-long assessment which estimated that more than $700 million worth of gold was being lost each year through illicit activity and identified 81 illegal mining sites.

The latest estimate is seven times lower. At the same time, the number of mining locations linked to the programme has increased to around 100.

The analysis asks a simple question: which number is accurate?

Without a published methodology, there is no way to test either claim. For a project requiring hundreds of billions of kwacha in public and private financing, that gap matters.

Mamico says it will need K85 billion to fund its first three months of operations and around K300 billion annually thereafter. The company has enlisted FDH Bank and NBS Bank as partners, but key parts of the commercial framework are still unresolved.

Most notably, the arrangement depends on an offtake agreement with the RBM that has yet to be concluded.

The uncertainty extends beyond the figures.

The analysis points to potential duplication between Mamico's planned operations and an existing RBM gold-purchasing initiative run through the Export Development Fund.

By September, that programme had already acquired about 1.63 tonnes of gold, raising questions about whether the government is creating parallel structures within the same market.

Close 

There is also a more fundamental challenge. Artisanal miners will only sell through official channels if they can secure competitive prices and prompt payment.

If unofficial traders offer better deals, the incentive to bypass the formal system remains intact, regardless of how many buying centres are established.

Yet the pressure to make the project work is immense.

Malawi's foreign exchange position remains fragile. Official reserves stood at $600.6 million in September, enough to cover just 2.4 months of imports, below the internationally recognised three-month benchmark.

Gold has emerged as one of the few commodities capable of generating substantial foreign currency earnings. In April alone, the RBM exported 589.95 kilogrammes of locally purchased gold valued at $75.09 million.

For ministers and policymakers, the allure is obvious: bring more gold into formal channels and bolster dwindling reserves.

But as Mtika's analysis suggests, the success of the strategy may hinge less on ambition than on transparency.

Until Mamico discloses how it calculated its smuggling estimates, clarifies how it will coexist with existing state-run gold programmes, and produces verifiable data on production, purchases and exports, the initiative will continue to face a credibility problem.

For now, the government's gold rush is asking the public to trust numbers it has yet to prove.

World.title: Somalia: Somalia's Govt Welcomes Election Timetable and Urges Political Dialogue
World.content:
Mogadishu — Somalia's federal government on Thursday welcomed an election timetable announced by the Independent National Electoral and Boundaries Commission, covering elections for both houses of parliament and the president.

In a statement dated October 15, 2026, the government described the timetable as an important step towards implementing the electoral process and strengthening democracy in the country.

The government said it had spent the past 18 months offering opportunities for consultation and negotiations aimed at helping Somali political stakeholders reach agreement on key national issues, particularly the electoral process.

It said the consultations would continue, adding that it remained committed to securing a broad-based understanding among the country's political actors.

The government described its support for the election timetable and its continued commitment to dialogue as complementary efforts that would help preserve stability, strengthen national unity and safeguard citizens' constitutional rights.

It called on all political stakeholders to engage in consultations in good faith and with a sense of national responsibility, urging them to work together to ensure peaceful elections that strengthen public confidence and Somalia's state institutions.

The statement comes amid political differences over Somalia's electoral process, including disagreements over the proposed arrangements and calls for an inclusive political agreement.

World.title: South Africa: Masemola Back As Police Commissioner After Ramaphosa Lifts Suspension
World.content:
Masemola was placed on precautionary suspension in April 2026 after appearing in court on charges linked to a R360-million police health services tender.

Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane has served as acting National Police Commissioner, and Ramaphosa says she served with distinction.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has lifted the suspension of National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola, who will resume his full duties on Monday, 19 October.

The Presidency made the announcement on Friday.

Ramaphosa and Masemola agreed in April 2026 that Masemola would be deemed to be on precautionary suspension. This followed his appearance in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court on charges of contravening the Public Finance Management Act. The charges were linked to a R360-million police health services tender awarded to Medicare24.



National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi ordered the charges to be withdrawn after a review found no reasonable prospects of a successful prosecution on 15 September. The Pretoria Magistrate's Court formally withdrew the charges on 22 September.

Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, the police's chief financial officer, was appointed acting National Police Commissioner when Masemola was suspended.

Ramaphosa thanked her and said she served with distinction in the interim.

"The President welcomes the National Police Commissioner on his return to his full duties," presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya said.

The South African Policing Union had urged Ramaphosa to lift the suspension after the charges were withdrawn. After the withdrawal, Masemola told the media that he had not heard from the president.

The National Prosecuting Authority has also referred the case to the oversight judge of the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption, to look into whether there was any malice behind the original charges.

World.title: Lesotho: Is Construction At the Lesotho Highlands Water Project Polluting Rivers?
World.content:
The Lesotho Highlands Development Authority will refer suspected pollution for testing. We previously revealed that Kopano Ke Matlaâs wastewater-treatment systems were found to be non-compliant, despite repeated warnings. The photo shows the Sekoai River and the tunnel access site.

The Lesotho Highlands Development Authority will refer suspected pollution for testing

A contractor responsible for work on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project was suspended for 18 days last year for dumping acidic and oily wastewater into nearby rivers and the Katse reservoir.

Now residents along the Sekoai River near a construction site are reporting seeing suspected pollution in the waterways.

The Lesotho Highlands Development Authority says it will refer evidence of suspected pollution to the project engineer for inspection and testing.

Concern continues about pollution flowing through the Sekoai River in Mokhotlong near a Lesotho Highlands Water Project construction site. The contractor responsible for the site was allowed to resume work last year following a suspension for dumping acidic and oily wastewater into nearby rivers and the Katse reservoir.



In May 2025, we reported that Kopano Ke Matla Joint Venture, which is building the Polihali transfer tunnel, was suspended for discharging oily and acidic wastewater into nearby rivers and the Katse reservoir. The reservoir supplies drinking water to South Africa. The suspension sent home 1,400 workers on the M42-billion (M1 = R1) project between Lesotho and South Africa.

During a visit to Mokhotlong in August, we observed wastewater discharging from Kopano Ke Matla's tunnel boring machine access adit at Polihali.

The perimeter fence is approximately ten metres from the river. Wastewater appeared to flow continuously from an outlet pipe onto the land before reaching the river.

On 7 September, residents of Tloha-re-Buoe said foamy water was seen flowing in the Sekoai River in the same tunnel access area.

Villager Thomello Ramotloenya said he went to the river that morning to graze his animals only to find foamy white bubbles in the river.

The Lesotho Highlands Development Authority (LHDA) has said it will refer the evidence of suspected pollution we collected to the project engineer for inspection and testing.

Previous wastewater-treatment failures

We previously revealed that the supervising engineers found Kopano Ke Matla's wastewater-treatment systems to be non-compliant, despite repeated warnings.

A suspension letter dated 5 May 2025 stated that the contractor had addressed only three of 26 issues identified as non-compliant. The concerns included missing effluent test results, a malfunctioning sulphuric acid dosing pump, high pH levels in treated water, and evidence of oil contamination.

The engineers had raised concerns about untreated construction wastewater being discharged into the Ntšupe River, untreated tunnel effluent in the Katse reservoir, and failures to maintain sewage and wastewater-treatment plants.

Responding to our questions, LHDA spokesperson Mpho Brown said the suspension "was a precautionary and corrective step, taken to address identified shortcomings in wastewater treatment before they could result in harm".

Work resumed on 25 May after the project engineer inspected the upgrades. Independent laboratory results confirmed that Kopano Ke Matla's treated effluent met the required standards, he said.

Brown said the contractor was required to upgrade the treatment system, including additional settling capacity and pH correction, revise its operating procedures, and appoint a qualified process specialist to run the plant.

"The contractor revised the wastewater treatment plant method statement to provide for additional clarifier capacity for primary settlement, a pH correction stage ahead of final discharge, and a firm commitment to specialist supervision of the plant. The revised method statement was approved by the engineer."

LHDA to refer suspected pollution for testing

Responding on behalf of Kopano Ke Matla, Brown said the discharge observed during our visit was part of the approved wastewater-treatment system.

"The outlet observed during your visit is the plant's designated discharge point. It is an approved and monitored part of the treatment system, through which only treated effluent is released. The LHDA has received no complaints or reports of foaming, discolouration or pollution of the Sekoai River linked to the works."

Brown noted that an inspection and tests had not yet been carried out.

Should non-compliant effluent quality be identified, Brown said the discharge would be stopped immediately and Kopano Ke Matla would be required to correct the cause before discharge resumed.

"The LHDA will take whatever further action the contract allows. The LHDA remains committed to transparency with the communities of the project area and to holding its contractors to the environmental standards the project requires."

Brown did not respond to follow-up questions.

SA minister raised concerns

In May 2025, South African Minister of Water and Sanitation Pemmy Majodina's office issued a statement expressing concern about reports of non-compliance over effluent discharge by a contractor responsible for constructing the Polihali transfer tunnel.

Referring to the May 2025 suspension, the minister said a meeting had been held with a South African delegation in the Lesotho Highlands Water Commission and the Trans-Caledon Tunnel Authority. "The suspension was prompted by persistent failures to meet treatment standards across multiple sites, despite prior warnings and formal Non-Conformance Reports emanating from concerns on the inadequate management and treatment of wastewater and effluent generated during tunnel construction activities."

Close 

The DA also called on Majodina in May 2025 to ask the Auditor-General to investigate financial and environmental concerns surrounding the project.

"Construction has again halted at LHW phase 2 due to a contractor polluting nearby rivers and the Katse Dam, contaminating crucial drinking water supplies with acidic wastewater. This irresponsible breach of environmental standards poses serious risks to the existing water supply, which millions of South Africans rely upon."

The DA stated that the project's financial and environmental integrity was essential to securing affordable water supplies across Gauteng, the Free State, the North West and beyond. "Municipalities already struggle with significant debts exceeding R28-billion owed to water boards. Further financial mismanagement and environmental setbacks could severely compromise water affordability and sustainability, intensifying local water crises."

This story was produced by MNN Centre for Investigative Journalism and syndicated by the IJ Hub on behalf of its member centre network in Southern Africa. It is co-published with GroundUp.

World.title: Rwanda: Kagame Calls for African Collaboration On F1 Grand Prix
World.content:
President Paul Kagame has called for African countries to work together to make Formula 1 African Grand Prix in Rwanda a success for the continent, following messages of support from South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema.

Responding to Ramaphosa's congratulations and offer of support on X, Kagame said Rwanda looked forward to working with other countries to make the event a continental achievement.

ALSO READ: African drivers welcome historic Rwanda-F1 Grand Prix deal

"We look forward to working with you and all who share this vision as we make this a truly African Grand Prix in every way possible, and take motorsport to new heights on our continent," Kagame said in the post.



Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema also congratulated Kagame and the people of Rwanda on securing hosting rights of the African Grand Prix, describing the Rwanda-Formula 1 agreement announced on Tuesday in Kigali as a historic achievement reflecting resilience, vision and hard work.

ALSO READ: Ramaphosa congratulates Rwanda on 10-year Formula 1 deal

"Zambia shares your pride in this milestone for Rwanda and Africa," Hichilema said.

In response, Kagame described the agreement as a milestone for both Rwanda and Africa, expressing his readiness to work with Hichilema and other African leaders to make the event a success for the entire continent.

"This is a milestone for Rwanda and for Africa, and we look forward to working with you and our African brothers and sisters to make the African Grand Prix a success for the entire continent," Kagame said.

The 10-year agreement will see Rwanda host a Formula 1 Grand Prix in the early 2030s on a circuit planned for construction in Bugesera. It will be the first to be hosted on the African continent since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.

World.title: Prince Harry's reported $100K deal for Princess Diana MasterClass sparks 'cash grab' claims from royal experts
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Prince Harry has spent years publicly unpacking his grief over the death of his mother, Princess Diana. But his latest revelations have sparked renewed skepticism among royal experts.

The Duke of Sussex opened up about how losing his mother when he was 12 affected his life in a new MasterClass course titled "Redefining Grief: Building Resilience Through Loss," which debuted Oct. 8.

In the course, Harry spoke with neuroscientist and grief expert Dr. Mary-Frances O'Connor about how grief can affect the brain and body.

PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE FEEDING THE 'PUBLICITY MACHINE' DESPITE PRIVACY DEMANDS: EXPERT

The Daily Mail reported that Harry pocketed $100,000, plus a share of subscription revenue for his class. A source told the outlet, "I'd encourage everyone to watch it before casting any judgment," adding that he should not be criticized at length for "speaking from the heart."

Forbes previously reported that most MasterClass instructors get at least $100,000 and a share of at least 30% of revenue.

The Daily Mail reported that a spokesperson confirmed Harry was paid by MasterClass but declined to comment further. Past stars featured on the platform include Martin Scorsese, Gordon Ramsay and Hillary Clinton, among others.

Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell and MasterClass for comment.

Several royal experts told Fox News Digital that Harry's decision to repeatedly revisit his grief through books, interviews and media projects has fueled debate over whether the 42-year-old is profiting from the tragedy he shares with his brother, Prince William, who has largely chosen to grieve outside the spotlight.

WATCH: PRINCE HARRY'S REPORTED PRINCESS DIANA MOVIE PROJECT SPARKS CONTROVERSY

"Prince Harry has spoken extensively about his emotional scars and unresolved grief surrounding the death of his mother," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital.

"However, Harry continuously paints himself a victim," Chard said. "Blame always falls on someone else. He realizes people's interest in Diana and, let's not forget, it makes a quick buck. It's seen as a cash grab, cashing in on his mother's death. It plays into the reported title 'Grief Grifter.'"

"The public understands the heartache Harry and William must have endured after their mother passed away," Chard said. "Grief affects people in different ways, and both boys endured divergent paths of grief."

According to People magazine, MasterClass approached Harry about developing a class on grief in 2025. The course was filmed in California during the summer of 2026, before Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, traveled back to the U.K.

People reported that the course, released ahead of World Mental Health Day on Oct. 10, supports two charities: Scotty's Little Soldiers, a U.K. organization that helps children and young people whose parents died during or after service in the British Armed Forces, and Comfort Zone Camp, a U.S. nonprofit that provides bereavement camps for grieving children.

According to The Times, William does not plan to make a film about Diana to mark the 30th anniversary of her death in 2027, in part to avoid further conflict with Harry. The outlet also reported that William has declined several offers to make or appear in documentaries about his mother.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Meanwhile, Harry is considering several projects to mark the 30th anniversary of Diana's death, according to People magazine. While several ideas are under discussion, the outlet reported that no documentary has been finalized or confirmed. Several sources told People that Harry has reached out to family members and friends of his late mother.

The class also arrived just weeks after Princess Diana's younger brother, Charles Spencer, released his memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister."

At the beginning of the course, Harry recalled his reaction to learning of his mother's death.

"I didn't cry when I was told my mom died, only at her burial, and then not again for nearly two decades," he said, as quoted by People. "I was convinced that was strength, but it wasn't. It was a 12-year-old boy with no permission to fall apart and no roadmap for how to heal."

"You would think I had the best help in the world," Harry said. "I'm a prince for God's sake. But I was still grieving and didn't have any place to put those feelings."

In his 2023 memoir, "Spare," Harry wrote that his father, King Charles III, didn't hug him after telling him Diana had died.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Pa didn't hug me," Harry wrote. "He wasn't great at showing emotions under normal circumstances. How could he be expected to show them in such a crisis? His hand did fall once more on my knee, and he said, 'It's going to be OK.' That was quite a lot for him. Fatherly, hopeful, kind. And so very untrue."

For some royal experts, however, the issue isn't whether Harry has a right to discuss his grief, but his decision to repeatedly revisit it publicly.

"Sadly, Harry hasn't dealt well at all with his grief," British royal expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital.

Fordwich echoed Chard's criticism, saying Harry has faced accusations of being a "grief grifter" for repeatedly discussing his mother's death through public projects that could generate revenue.

"What mother would want her child to be miserable and mourning so many years later?" Fordwich asked.

Other royal commentators see Harry's decision differently. Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital that Harry is using his platform to raise awareness of mental health issues and encourage others to discuss their experiences and seek help.

"I feel this is not a ploy on his part to create attention or sympathy from the public," Turner said. "I see it as an act of bravery on his part to distance himself from former royal trappings and show himself as most people see him: a man of the people."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Harry also said he spent years feeling that experiencing happiness would mean betraying his mother's memory.

"I'd spent so long emotionally numb, to a large extent, because I felt disloyal and guilty for the possibility of being happy and joyful without her," Harry said. "I felt like I had to be sad, and I had to be emotionally numb in order to prove to her that I missed her."

"But the reality is, what I discovered was actually she just wanted me to be happy," Harry said. "And that was a huge mental shift for me. It freed me, and it gave me a whole different outlook on life."

In the course, Harry also described his experience after moving to Canada with his wife, Meghan Markle, and their son, Prince Archie, in late 2019. The couple stepped back from their roles as senior working royals in 2020, citing intrusive British media coverage and a lack of support from the palace as reasons for their departure.

Harry said he experienced an "adrenaline crash."

"We moved to Canada to get some space away from everything, just to be able to think," Harry said. "Being in Canada, away from the stressful environment where presumably my body was just pumped full of adrenaline, within two or three days, I experienced this adrenaline crash — something that I'd never experienced before."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"It was as if I needed stress in order to get the adrenaline to make my brain function because I became useless around the house," Harry said. "I actually slipped into depression for about two weeks and I felt like I couldn't function without adrenaline."

Harry's disclosure that he experienced depression shortly after leaving royal life caught Chard's attention.

"The new narrative that he was depressed for a couple of weeks after leaving the British royal family is slightly suspect and does not resonate with his 'Freedom Flight,'" Chard said. "Harry wears his heart on his sleeve, and many doubt he'd forgotten to state this information in his previous memoir, documentaries and interviews."

"This is definitely new information and slightly changes the narrative," Chard said.

Harry also said that carrying out royal duties triggered anxiety and panic attacks.

"There was a time where public engagements just created absolute panic right from beginning to end," Harry said. "The panic was having to put my suit, jacket, and tie on and suddenly feel suffocated. The panic was going from A to B, getting out of the car in front of all the cameras and the clicks.

PRINCE WILLIAM ‘INCANDESCENT WITH ANGER’ AT PRINCE HARRY AS DIANA ANNIVERSARY DEEPENS ROYAL RIFT: PIERS MORGAN

"I started to realize that I had become seriously depleted when just putting a simple dress shirt on — the tightening of the collar — literally felt like I was suffocating, and I would be experiencing panic attacks just in the car on the way to work," Harry said. "And that's when I realized, OK, there's something bigger, there's something else that you need to look into here."

Royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital he believes Harry will continue discussing Diana's death if he moves forward with a documentary about his mother.

"There is no doubt he is likely to continue emphasizing his vulnerability after Princess Diana's death," Fitzwilliams said. "We saw the emotional Harry on MasterClass, yet again."

Harry also credited therapy with helping him confront grief he had carried for decades.

"I learned more about myself in two or three sessions than I had done in 20 years," Harry said. "First of all, she helped me accept and acknowledge that I was grieving and that it was okay to grieve and that what happened to me was really quite hard."

Nearly three decades after Diana's death, Harry and William continue to take different approaches to honoring their mother's memory — one through public revelations, the other largely away from the spotlight.

World.title: Former Border Patrol chief recalls Biden migrant surge chaos as Trump crackdown delivers historic turnaround
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

President Donald Trump’s border crackdown has sharply reduced the illegal crossings that overwhelmed agents under former President Joe Biden, with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) reporting Thursday historic lows in apprehensions and a full fiscal year without Border Patrol releasing migrants into the country.

For retired Yuma Arizona Sector U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Border Patrol Chief Chris Clem, the turnaround stands in sharp contrast to days when his agents could not pick up migrants fast enough and the consequences spilled into neighborhoods, farms and local businesses.

"They just started walking through the agriculture fields. They started running through town," Clem told Fox News Digital, recalling the surge in December 2021. "They started going to the food bank. They started knocking on people’s doors at all hours of the nights."

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

But while Clem said he credits stronger enforcement and the prospect of deportation with helping drive the decline, he warned that the gains could face another threat — a political shift in Washington.

"There are a lot of policy decisions that can be really jammed up by a Congress that’s gung-ho to overturn what this president has done," said Clem, who warned that changes in congressional control could complicate enforcement through funding decisions and policy restrictions, while a future presidential administration could pursue broader reversals.

Preliminary DHS figures released Thursday show Border Patrol recorded 98,708 southwest border apprehensions in fiscal year 2026, roughly 95% below the annual average of more than 1.8 million during the Biden administration.

That translates to about 270 apprehensions a day across the southwest border, compared with roughly 5,000 using the department’s Biden-era annual average.

In Yuma alone, Clem recalled daily arrivals climbing from roughly 25 in December 2020, to more than 1,000 by December 2021. During a particularly difficult three-day stretch that month, he said, daily arrivals approached 1,500.

TRUMP HITS DRAMATIC MILESTONE IN MASSIVE DEPARTURE FROM BIDEN BORDER PLAN: 'WHAT A DIFFERENCE'

Weather problems and a shortage of resources compounded the strain, leaving agents struggling to transport people from the border, he said.

"That was really when it, you know, was the most critical for me because we had the true community impact of a failed border security policy out of Washington, D.C.," Clem said.

His agents remained committed to the mission, he said, but the volume was overwhelming.

"The agents, their heads were in the right place. They knew they had to do the job," Clem said. "But when you’re outnumbered, literally 100 to one, it’s very difficult."

The new DHS figures put an entire fiscal year of southwest border apprehensions below half the 249,740 recorded during the Biden administration’s single busiest month.

DHS also said September marked the 17th consecutive month without Border Patrol releasing migrants into the country, completing what it described as the agency’s first full fiscal year with zero releases.

DHS TOUTS MILLIONS OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT DEPARTURES AS BORDER CROSSINGS DROP 94% UNDER TRUMP

Clem said the prospect of being released had given smugglers a powerful selling point during the previous administration.

"If you get to the border, you’re gonna be processed, and you’ll be let go," he said, describing the pitch.

He argued that changing that expectation is central to discouraging illegal crossings.

"They know that they’re not gonna be processed and released, which was the status quo under the Biden-Harris administration," Clem said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

He credited a combination of personnel, infrastructure, technology and consequences for illegal entry, rather than any single measure.

The enforcement effort also extends beyond the border itself.

Clem said U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations inside the country add another layer, making clear that getting past Border Patrol does not eliminate the possibility of arrest and removal.

"When you combine the strong border posture, as well as the strong and robust interior enforcement, it’s a recipe for success," he said.

Border czar Tom Homan pointed to that interior enforcement push Thursday, saying ICE had recorded its highest single-day deportation total since Trump returned to office.

TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

"We are deportation-maxxing—firing on all cylinders while still expanding our capabilities to ramp up removals beyond current record-breaking levels," Homan wrote on social media.

Homan said he visited ICE Air Operations in Alexandria, Louisiana, to observe removal operations, including a flight returning Haitians he said had criminal records involving aggravated assault, sexual assault, kidnapping, battery and other offenses.

He also said ICE conducted more removals in September than in any other month, though his post did not provide totals or specify the comparison period. Fiscal year 2026 figures were still being finalized, he said.

The ICE removal figures measure a separate part of the immigration system from Border Patrol apprehensions and releases.

"President Trump promised the American people a secure border, and the data proves he delivered," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement announcing the border figures. "The results could not be clearer: strong enforcement works."

Still, Clem cautioned that lower numbers do not eliminate threats from smugglers or people trying to evade detection.

"There are always gonna be that risk where somebody does sneak through. Who is that person?" he said.

He argued that mixed political messages can also give smugglers an opening to lure people into dangerous journeys with promises that U.S. policies will change.

"When our policies aren’t clear and transparent, and we’re not holding ourselves accountable, it’s a marketing tool for the smuggling organizations," he said.

For Clem, the distinction between debating immigration policy and maintaining border security is essential.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We have an immigration issue we need to address," he said. "We need to find a way to retain and recruit those that are here, that are foreign nationals that want to contribute."

"But none of that should matter when it comes down to securing the border," Clem added. "We should always be looking at keeping America safe."

World.title: Texas woman sentenced to 7 years in prison, annual jail time during probation for deadly DUI crash
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Texas woman convicted of killing a college student in a drunken-driving crash was sentenced to seven years in prison and ordered to return to jail for 15 days each year while on probation.

Lynlee Pollis, 30, was sentenced Wednesday after being convicted of intoxication manslaughter and intoxication assault in the September 2023 crash that killed 19-year-old Southern Methodist University student Honor Wallace and seriously injured her friend, Catherine "CeCe" Solberg, according to The Dallas Morning News.

State District Judge Jennifer Balido also ordered Pollis to serve 10 years of probation following her release from prison, including 15 days in jail annually.

Some of the required jail dates coincide with the victims' birthdays, Pollis' birthday and the anniversary of the deadly crash, according to the newspaper.

NEVADA PAROLE BOARD REJECTS HENRY RUGGS III'S BID FOR EARLY RELEASE AFTER DEADLY 156 MPH DUI CRASH

The sentence came after roughly three hours of jury deliberations following a two-and-a-half-week trial.

During the trial, Solberg's father, Bobby Solberg, delivered an emotional victim impact statement criticizing Pollis for putting the families through the lengthy proceedings.

"You were so drunk and you wouldn’t admit it. You made us sit through this [trial] for three weeks," Solberg said. "We’ve seen no personal accountability from you."

PROMINENT BUSINESSMAN LEARNS FATE IN BOAT CRASH CASE THAT KILLED TEEN, MAIMED ANOTHER

Wallace's father, David Wallace, also confronted Pollis in his victim impact statement.

"You took the most precious gift from us through your selfishness," he said. "Own it. Own what you did."

On Sept. 24, 2023, Wallace was driving her Volkswagen Jetta through a green light in Dallas when Pollis' Lexus SUV slammed into her vehicle.

Wallace was pronounced dead at the hospital, while Solberg, a passenger in the Jetta, suffered a shoulder injury and concussion. She was later diagnosed with a traumatic brain injury, according to The Dallas Morning News.

DRUNK REPEAT OFFENDER CALLED A 'TICKING TIME-BOMB' BEFORE 80-MPH BOATING COLLISION KILLED WOMAN: PROSECUTORS

According to testimony from prosecution experts cited by the newspaper, Pollis was traveling approximately 67 mph in a 35-mph zone and drove through a traffic light that had been red for at least five seconds.

Pollis' husky named Tequila, who was also in the vehicle, was not hurt.

The newspaper reported that testing showed Pollis had a blood alcohol concentration of 0.294%, nearly four times Texas' legal limit of 0.08%.

According to the initial arrest affidavit, officers noticed Pollis had glassy eyes, slurred speech and an odor of alcohol when they interviewed her at the hospital.

Her attorneys had sought probation rather than prison, pointing to her lack of prior felony convictions.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Defense attorney Scott Palmer said during his closing argument that Pollis was a "good person who made a terrible decision."

World.title: Illegal alien busted allegedly hauling enough fentanyl to potentially kill state’s entire population — twice
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

An illegal immigrant pulled over for speeding in Nevada allegedly had enough fentanyl in his truck to kill millions, federal prosecutors say.

Francisco Joel Garcia Farias, 26, now faces federal drug-trafficking charges after a Lincoln County sheriff’s deputy stopped his pickup on a rural highway and a narcotics detection dog alerted to the vehicle, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.

Inside, authorities say they found 13 large storage totes packed with approximately 30 pounds of suspected fentanyl and 677 pounds of suspected methamphetamine, a combined haul of more than 700 pounds.

CALIFORNIA K-9 OTIS HELPS POLICE SEIZE 440 POUNDS OF COCAINE DURING ALHAMBRA TRAFFIC STOP

"The massive scale of this seizure underscores the staggering volume of illicit narcotics flowing into our communities from transnational criminal organizations," said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada.

"Fourteen kilograms of fentanyl alone represents approximately seven million potentially lethal two-milligram doses — enough to kill more than twice the population of Nevada — and, when combined with over 650 pounds of methamphetamine, represents an estimated street value of approximately $2 million," Chattah said.

AS A US ATTORNEY, I SEE FENTANYL'S HORRIFYING TOLL UP CLOSE. CONGRESS MUST ACT NOW

Based on that lethal-dose estimate, the fentanyl could potentially kill nearly twice the population of Los Angeles, everyone in Indiana, or roughly the entire population of Paraguay.

"These staggering quantities reflect a blatant disregard for human life, driven purely by profit," Chattah said.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF FENTANYL DEALING LINKED TO VIRGINIA HIGH SCHOOL OVERDOSES

The Justice Department identified Garcia Farias as an illegal immigrant in its announcement of the charges.

The bust began Oct. 13 on U.S. Highway 93 near Ash Springs, Nevada, when a deputy saw the pickup traveling above the posted speed limit, according to prosecutors’ account of the criminal complaint.

HERO K-9 SNIFFS OUT HIDDEN $6M COCAINE SHIPMENT ALONG US-CANADA BORDER

After the dog alerted, deputies searched the truck and uncovered numerous vacuum-sealed packages inside the totes.

Authorities recovered approximately 187 packages of a white crystalline substance weighing about 307.22 kilograms, along with 13 brick-shaped packages weighing approximately 14 kilograms. Field tests of selected samples were positive for methamphetamine and fentanyl, respectively, prosecutors said.

DOJ ANNOUNCES 81 ALLEGED GANG MEMBERS INDICTED AFTER PUERTO RICO DRUG TRAFFICKING TAKEDOWN

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the seizure kept a potentially deadly drug supply off American streets.

"Anyone who plans to release a deadly drug like fentanyl onto American streets will be prosecuted," Blanche said. "Thanks to the diligent work of federal and local law enforcement, the lethal drugs allegedly possessed by this illegal alien are no longer endangering the lives of countless Americans."

CBP OFFICERS SEIZE $67 MILLION IN ILLEGAL DRUGS AT SAN DIEGO BORDER PORTS, DHS SAYS

The investigation involved Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office, and Homeland Security Task Force partners.

"The suspected fentanyl and methamphetamine seized in this case represent an extraordinary threat to public safety," said John A. Condon, executive associate director of HSI.

"Through close coordination with the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office, the U.S. Attorney’s Office, and our Homeland Security Task Force partners, HSI will continue to identify, investigate and hold accountable those who profit from poisoning Americans and endangering our communities," Condon said.

Lincoln County Sheriff Derek Foremaster credited his deputies’ traffic enforcement and the trained dog with uncovering the suspected narcotics.

DOJ TOUTS HUNDREDS OF GUN, DRUG ARRESTS AS ST LOUIS SURGE OPERATION ENDS: 'VIOLENCE IS NOT INEVITABLE'

"The allegations in this case underscore the serious threat illicit narcotics pose to rural communities and the traveling public," Foremaster said.

"I am proud of the vigilance and professionalism demonstrated by our deputies, whose proactive traffic enforcement and trained K-9 deployment led to the identification of suspected narcotics and a coordinated response with Homeland Security Investigations."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Garcia Farias is charged with possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of a mixture containing fentanyl and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture containing methamphetamine.

If convicted, he faces a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison and a maximum of life on each count, followed by five years of supervised release, according to prosecutors.

World.title: Alleged Chinese agent has ties to scam group, records show
World.content:
A California realtor charged with working as a Chinese agent has connections to an alleged Cambodian criminal organization accused of using forced labor to run multibillion-dollar scams targeting Americans, a CBS News investigation reveals.

Last week, the FBI charged Irvine realtor Wanying "Heather" Zhang, 34, with operating as an unregistered foreign agent after they allegedly caught her surveilling the Taiwanese president's son in Seattle in 2025. She was accompanied by a travel companion whom CBS News has identified as Fatai Miao, 54.

Both Zhang and Miao have links to individuals involved in sprawling criminal enterprises, according to several federal court filings reviewed by CBS News.

The web of connections provides a rare glimpse into the multi-faceted dealings of a woman who federal agents have alleged spent years engaged in intelligence work on U.S. soil for the Chinese government.

During her time in California, Zhang appears to have traveled in wealthy circles, posing for photos on the Chinese social media site Xiaohongshu in a Bugatti sports car. She wrote that the car belonged to her friend. The car appears to be owned by a man described by the Justice Department as the "enforcer" in an alleged multibillion-dollar fraud ring fueled by modern slavery.

Zhang shared this photo on her social media in a car belonging to Prince Group alleged "enforcer" Chen Sokly. Wanying Zhang / Xiaohongshu.com

The U.S. government claims international conglomerate the Prince Group conducted at least $15 billion of online scams targeting Americans, using workers in at least 10 alleged forced labor camps in Cambodia.

Zhang also forged a yearslong relationship with Miao, who is the registered agent and organizer for Yuanjin Development & Construction LLC, located at a five-bedroom home on Interstellar Street in Irvine.

Miao, a construction entrepreneur, has a business registered at the home, a $4.5 million suburban house in Irvine, that prosecutors claim was also used as a "stash house" for an alleged Chinese money laundering organization. That operation allegedly worked in concert with the Sinaloa Cartel, according to a criminal complaint filed in 2023.

Miao was not charged or named in that complaint.

Drug Enforcement Administration task force officer Steven Gonzalez tracked a member of an alleged "large money laundering organization" dropping off a "red, medium-sized weighted tote bag" at the home on March 1, 2023, according to an affidavit in the criminal complaint.

"I believe, based upon my training and experience, my knowledge of this investigation, and conversations with agents experienced in money laundering techniques, that [the man] had just picked up and made a delivery of United States currency that was the proceeds of illicit activity," the DEA agent wrote in the May 2023 complaint.

It was one of several bag drops at stash houses around Los Angeles and Orange counties alleged by the DEA.

A defendant in the cartel money laundering case deposits alleged drug trafficking cash at an ATM, according to the DEA. U.S. Department of Justice

Miao has not been charged with any offense. Just days before the FBI broke down his door executing a search warrant in Irvine, he flew to China last month on a one-way ticket, prosecutors said.

The alleged crime gang was accused by the Justice Department of operating an unlicensed currency exchange to launder millions of dollars for the Sinaloa Cartel.

A federal prosecutor claimed during Zhang's second court hearing last Wednesday that she too had been operating an "unlicensed currency exchange" business, with $190,000 in profits sent to her Chinese bank account — though the government made no mention of the alleged drug ring in court or in any public filings concerning Zhang.

A separate indictment filed against 24 members of the group in April 2024 includes photographs from federal seizures showing stacks of $100 bills and truckfuls of bricks of cocaine and methamphetamine.

Top: Agents say they seized this bag of cash in January 2021. Bottom: DEA agents say they seized over 110 lbs of drugs containing cocaine in one bust as part of their investigation. U.S. Department of Justice

Group members had nicknames including "Ocean," "Batman" and "Dr. P."

An alleged leader of the organization was arrested on May 12, 2023, telling a DEA agent that he had 10 to 20 people on his team and that "most of the funds he sells come from fraud schemes," the agent wrote in the affidavit.

"He later admitted that he had previously dealt in drug proceeds through 2020, but said that it was 'scary,' because of the consequences from 'the Mexicans' if any funds were lost," the agent wrote.

Probe into international scam operation

Miao's business partner in Yuanjin Development, Cheng Zhang, is also business partners with the alleged "enforcer" of the Prince Group, a Cambodia-based organization accused by U.S. prosecutors of using forced labor to steal billions of dollars through scams and launder the proceeds.

California corporation Big Bow LLC is managed by both Cheng Zhang and another firm, M Capital Global California LLC, which is controlled by alleged Prince Group "enforcer" Chen Sokly.

CBS News has identified Sokly as the man named only as "Co-Conspirator-2" in an indictment against Prince Group chairman Chen Zhi filed in New York last year.

Chen Sokly, filmed at a yacht showcase. 9tro

The indictment calls Prince Group "one of the largest transnational criminal organizations in Asia," which "made enormous profits for Chen and his associates by operating forced-labor scam compounds across Cambodia that engaged in cryptocurrency investment fraud schemes."

"Thousands of migrant workers traveled to Cambodia and elsewhere seeking job opportunities but instead were trafficked and forced to work in scam compounds executing cryptocurrency investment fraud and other fraudulent schemes, often under the threat of violence," the indictment says. "The scam compounds housed vast dormitories surrounded by high walls and barbed wire, and functioned as forced labor camps."

Prosecutors say the Prince Group used this "phone farm" to run scams. U.S. Department of Justice

The federal crackdown on the group involved a seizure of $15 billion in bitcoin, which the Justice Department said was the biggest in its history.

The Prince Group has denied the claims and called the crackdown an "asset grab dressed up as law enforcement."

The indictment said "Co-Conspirator-2" used "corrupt and violent means to maintain Prince Group's dominance among scam operators," including allegedly buying a $3 million yacht for a foreign government official as a bribe.

The indictment also said "Co-Conspirator-2 served as Chairman of Awesome Global," a Prince Group subsidiary. Corporate records show a Cambodian firm by that name, listing both Chen Zhi and Chen Sokly as chairmen.

Sokly was first identified as Co-Conspirator-2 by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, an international nonprofit, on Aug. 8.

The alleged Chinese agent Wanying "Heather" Zhang also has links to the alleged crime ring enforcer Sokly.

In 2024 she posted a photo on Chinese social media site Xiaohongshu showing herself sitting in the driver's seat of a Bugatti Chiron, with the caption, "check out my friend's luxury car!"

The photo was taken down this week.

The car belonged to Wenzhi "Wesley" Fei, a self-described "poker degenerate" and cryptocurrency trader, according to his social media posts.

But in an interview with CBS News, Fei said he does not own the car. He said he borrowed it from Sokly, who he described as a "friend" and a "generous gentleman." He said he knows "nothing" about Chen's business dealings or the Prince Group.

Videos and photos shared on social media show Fei with Sokly in a garage with rare, luxury sports cars, and Fei posing in front of a 71-foot yacht imported by Sokly from Singapore, according to customs records.

Left: Fei poses on Sokly's yacht in a video he posted to Instagram. Right: Sokly's yacht, Susan. Wenzhi Fei / Instagram

He also posted on his Instagram page a video showing him climbing into a Ferrari sports car parked in the driveway of a Yorba Linda, California, home belonging to Brendon Luo, who was sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury for his involvement in the Prince Group.

In 2024 Fei organized a luxury "yacht event" for cryptocurrency industry members through his trading company, Block Infinity, at a Prince Group-owned tower in Singapore where chairman Chen Zhi had a $16 million suite.

Fei told CBS News he did not attend the event, that he does not know Wanying "Heather" Zhang, and that he and Sokly "were not that close."

"He's hard to contact after the allegations" against Prince Group by the Justice Department, Fei said.

Fei has not been charged with any crimes. Zhang has not been charged with any crimes other than acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government, and neither she nor Fei have been connected to the Prince Group or cartel money laundering in any federal law enforcement filings.

Zhang is a common Chinese last name and so Wanying Zhang may not be related to Miao's business partner Cheng Zhang or alleged cartel money launderer Sai Zhang.

Sokly did not respond to a request for comment sent to his California company.

"Mr. Chen and his companies were not a criminal syndicate but a collection of legitimate businesses serving millions of people and employing tens of thousands of people across the globe," a Prince Group spokesperson told OCCRP in June.

"Chen Zhi and the Prince Group of companies are innocent of the wild and unfounded accusations made by the U.S government, parroted in jurisdictions around the world."

Contacted by phone, Miao's son said his father did not want to comment, and added that he did not believe his father knew about his business address' links to alleged organized crime groups. He said Miao remains in China after flying there on a one-way ticket three weeks ago.

World.title: With Tesla Roadster debut, Elon Musk shows "flying cars are real"
World.content:
Houston — Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a "flying" car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company's facility on Thursday.

Technical and regulatory challenges have so far prevented the much-hyped flying car sector from getting off the ground.

Musk revealed Tesla's new Roadster sports car during a launch event at a SpaceX test facility in Texas.

During the demo, which was livestreamed on Tesla's X account, the car launched from a ramp that curled over so the vehicle was upside down, appearing to defy gravity by clinging to the surface before flying off the end, and then rolled over 180 degrees midair to land on its wheels.

Tesla unveiled its long-delayed new Roadster — which took flight using high-pressure gas boosters — at a launch event in Waco, Texas, Oct. 15, 2026, as seen in a photo taken from video provided by the company. Tesla/Handout via REUTERS

"Flying cars are real," Musk said during the event, adding that the vehicle's "success is not guaranteed" but "it will probably work."

Musk said the car was equipped with "ultra high-pressure air tanks" to propel itself into the air.

The tech billionaire described the development as "what happens when you have a collaboration with the world's best car company and the world's best rocket company," referring to Tesla and SpaceX.

The vehicle would go into production in 2028, he said.

American aviation pioneer Glenn Curtiss debuted the first flying car prototype in 1917.

But successful designs have become more seriously contemplated only in recent years as electric motors and high-performance batteries have advanced.

Musk, who has appeared to have a close but sometimes tumultuous relationship with President Trump, has thrust his companies to the forefront of several major industries, and he continues pushing into new ones.

SpaceX announced a week ago that it had agreed to buy licenses for radio airwaves that will enable its Starlink Mobile satellite business to provide cellular service inside buildings, a move the company said would allow it to "become a major mobile carrier in the U.S."

"This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," Musk said in an Oct. 8 social media post.

World.title: Musk donates over $150 million to Senate GOP group, assisting Paxton
World.content:
Billionaire Elon Musk donated $158 million last month to the main super PAC supporting Senate Republicans, which almost immediately sent the money to a group that supports GOP Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

Republicans are fighting to hold on to the Texas Senate seat, as polls point to a tight race between Paxton and Democratic opponent James Talarico.

The assist from Musk — along with tens of millions of dollars in donations to other groups — marks a decisive return to large-scale political giving for the world's richest man, who spent over a quarter of a billion dollars backing President Trump and other Republican candidates in 2024.

Musk donated $75 million to the Senate Leadership Fund PAC on Sept. 9, and $83 million two weeks later, the group reported Thursday. Combined, the two super-sized donations from Musk made up more than half of the super PAC's total receipts in the third quarter of this year.

One day after each donation, the Senate Leadership Fund PAC disbursed the same amount to Texas PAC. That group reported over $100 million in pro-Paxton and anti-Talarico spending.

Musk also donated more than $80 million from July to September to his own group, America PAC, which was the primary vehicle for his political giving in 2024. The group reported spending on the Texas Senate contest and several other competitive congressional races.

Musk — who has strongly criticized Talarico in recent weeks — is a resident of Texas, and his largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla, base many of their operations in the state.

Talarico is attempting to become the first Democrat to win a statewide race in Texas in more than three decades. He has sought to capitalize on Paxton's history of scandal, and on still-lingering divides among Texas Republicans after Paxton defeated incumbent Republican Sen. John Cornyn in a bitter primary contest earlier this year. Paxton and his allies, including Mr. Trump, have argued Talarico is too far to the left for Texas' electorate.

Most recent polls show Talarico with a within-the-margin-of-error lead. If Paxton loses the seat, it could deal a serious blow to Republicans' efforts to hold on to the Senate.

After Musk served as the country's top political donor in the 2024 cycle, it was initially unclear whether he planned to spend similar sums in future elections. His stint leading the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency ended with him briefly feuding with the president, and he suggested at one point last year that he planned to scale back his political spending, joking during one interview, "I think I've done enough."

America PAC spokesperson Andrew Romeo said in a statement to CBS News: "If Democrats take control of Washington and win key gubernatorial and attorney general races this November, then America risks becoming a socialist, woke and borderless country. These robust investments have allowed the G.O.P. apparatus to get its message out so Republicans can have a fighting chance to defy history."
