How the War Began in April 2023

The army is the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), commanded by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. Its rival, the RSF, is a paramilitary force that answers to Hemedti.

The two men co-led a military takeover in October 2021 that ended Sudan’s civilian-led transition, the US Treasury said in January 2025. They turned on each other in April 2023, and the UN calls the RSF the army’s former ally.

A UN Panel of Experts report of April 2025 found that, by July 2024, Burhan still refused to engage with the RSF. It added that the RSF had not met the withdrawal protocols of the Jeddah Declaration of May 2023.

This Sudan war explained guide sits beside our Sudan in the Horn of Africa profile of the country. Sudan has about 51.7 million people, the World Bank estimated for 2025, and a coast on the Red Sea.

Who Controls What in 2026

Crisis Group wrote in February 2026 that the army controls Khartoum and most of Sudan’s centre and east, which includes Port Sudan on the Red Sea coast. Security Council Report said in October 2026 that the army also holds the reopened corridor between Khartoum and El Obeid.

The RSF took El Fasher, the army’s last major stronghold in Darfur, on 26 October 2025 after an 18-month siege, UN News reported. In a report of 3 September 2026, UN investigators said conduct during the takeover displayed hallmarks of genocide.

Fighting has since moved to Kordofan, which the UN-backed hunger monitor IPC calls the epicentre of Sudan’s conflict. More than 300,000 people have been forced from their homes there since October 2025, it said on 12 October 2026.

El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, lives under siege-like conditions, Security Council Report said in October 2026. The RSF keeps striking the city with drones while the army holds the road to Khartoum.

In Blue Nile, the RSF and an allied armed group, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, recaptured Kurmuk and Geissan in mid-August 2026. Ed Damazin, the state capital, came under assault on 4 September, Security Council Report said.

Army (SAF) Leader: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan Holds: Khartoum, the Khartoum to El Obeid corridor, and most of the centre and east Rapid Support Forces (RSF) Leader: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti Holds: El Fasher in North Darfur and parts of West Kordofan Contested Fronts: El Obeid and North Kordofan, South Kordofan, and Blue Nile

Women at a market in Khartoum, the Sudanese capital that the army holds. (Photo: Dr. Ondřej Havelka, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Human Toll

The International Organization for Migration counts 8.6 million people displaced inside Sudan, UN News reported in September 2026. Darfur hosts 65 percent of them, and more than 700,000 shelter in Tawila alone.

The UN refugee agency’s statistics show about 3.8 million Sudanese refugees and asylum seekers abroad at the end of 2025. Chad hosted about 1.33 million of them, Egypt about 834,000, Libya about 639,000 and South Sudan about 571,000.

The IPC found in May 2026 that nearly 19.5 million people, about 41 percent of Sudan, faced crisis-level hunger or worse. Nearly 135,000 were in Catastrophe, its worst phase, and 14 areas of Darfur and South Kordofan faced a risk of famine.

On 12 October 2026 the IPC warned of rising famine risk in Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, where drought now covers more than half of Sudan. Surveys of two camps in Eastern Jebel Marra found acute malnutrition among children at 38 and 30.8 percent, above the famine threshold.

On 9 October 2026 a drone strike near a displacement camp in Blue Nile killed at least 30 people, Sudan Tribune reported. Local authorities blamed the RSF, which did not immediately respond.

As of 8 October 2026, less than half of the humanitarian appeal for Sudan had been funded, UN News said. The IPC’s Famine Review Committee called the situation a humanitarian catastrophe of historic proportions.

The Outside Backers

Outside support keeps both sides supplied, the UN’s independent Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan said on 3 September 2026. It found reasonable grounds to believe that the army used foreign-supplied drones in operations that harmed civilians.

It found reasonable grounds to believe recruiters in Colombia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) supplied the RSF through Chad, southeastern Libya and Bosaso, Somalia. It documented up to 2,000 former Colombian military contractors working with RSF drones and artillery.

Human Rights Watch alleged in May 2026 that the UAE played a role in deploying Colombian fighters to the RSF. The UAE has said it categorically rejects any claims of providing any form of support to either warring party.

Crisis Group wrote in February 2026 that the UAE is the RSF’s chief sponsor, and that Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Eritrea favour the army. It added that the army accuses Ethiopia of helping the RSF, including through an alleged RSF training camp in Benishangul-Gumuz.

On 4 October 2026 the leaders of Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia adopted the El Alamein Joint Declaration on Red Sea governance, Security Council Report said. Our guides to Eritrea and Somalia cover two of those capitals.

Russia, China, Pakistan and the three African members of the Security Council wanted the Darfur arms embargo renewed without widening it. The United States wanted it extended to all of Sudan, and on 8 October 2026 the Council adopted a two-month rollover.

Backing the army Egypt: Close wartime ally, reported by Crisis Group (2026) Saudi Arabia: Favours the army, reported by Crisis Group (2026) Eritrea: Sided with the army and trained allied militias, reported by Crisis Group (2026) Backing the RSF UAE: Called the RSF’s chief sponsor by Crisis Group (2026); alleged, and the UAE denies it Colombia and UAE networks: Reasonable grounds to believe they supplied fighters and weapons, documented by the UN mission (2026) Ethiopia: Military and logistical help alleged by the army (2025 and 2026); no independent finding

Why It Matters for the Red Sea

Sudan’s coast and its main port, Port Sudan, sit on the shipping lane that our Bab el-Mandeb analysis describes. Russia and Sudan signed a preliminary naval base deal in late 2020, but a military source told Sudan Tribune in December 2025 that Sudan had frozen it.

Egypt hosts about 834,000 Sudanese refugees and asylum seekers by the UN refugee agency’s end-2025 count. Human Rights Watch reported in July 2026 that Egypt arrested and deported some of them, while our guide to Ethiopia shows how that neighbour is pulled in.

Chad hosts the most refugees, and Crisis Group wrote on 28 August 2026 that Chad blames Sudan’s army for strikes on a convoy. On 10 October 2026 a strike near the Ethiopian border reportedly killed 41 displaced people.

Our report on the Blue Nile drone strike covers the 9 October attack. Burhan’s ties with Eritrea are the subject of our report on his visit to Asmara.

Workers load donated wheat onto trucks at Port Sudan, Sudan’s main Red Sea port, in a photo from the 2000s. (Photo: USAID, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

Peace Efforts

The Geneva talks of 16 to 23 August 2024, organised by Saudi Arabia and the United States, did not end the fighting. The army declined to attend, the UN Panel of Experts reported.

The main diplomatic track is the Quad, made up of the United States, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Security Council Report expects it to meet the Quintet, a group of African, European, Arab and UN bodies, in Switzerland on 20 and 21 October 2026.

Washington has proposed a 90-day humanitarian truce to be agreed without preconditions, Sudan Tribune reported on 15 October 2026. The army has resisted it, and on the same day Burhan sent a message to President Donald Trump saying Sudan is committed to US-sponsored peace efforts.

The army wants the RSF to leave the cities it occupies before or alongside any truce, a Sudan Tribune analysis wrote on 21 September 2026. The RSF backs a humanitarian truce but objects to parts of the withdrawal plan.

The US reportedly withheld a visa for Burhan ahead of his address to the UN General Assembly in September 2026, Security Council Report said. The Secretary-General said he was deeply concerned that it had not been issued.

What the Markets Say

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Polymarket’s market on a Sudan civil war ceasefire gives an 11.5% chance of one by 31 December 2026 (16 October, 5:17 a.m. ET). The event has drawn about US$120,000 in bets, and the December contract alone about US$15,000.

A separate Polymarket market gives a 12.0% chance that Eritrea invades Ethiopia by 31 December 2026, with about US$99,000 wagered. Crisis Group warned in February 2026 that such a war would overlap with Sudan’s, as our pillar guide to Horn of Africa geopolitics explains.

What It Means for US Readers

For US readers the Sudan war explained here matters first as a sanctions story. The Treasury sanctioned Hemedti on 7 January 2025 and Burhan on 16 January 2025, and Human Rights Watch notes it targeted the Colombian recruitment network in December 2025.

Washington leads the drafting of the Sudan sanctions text at the Security Council. Companies and banks with Gulf, Egyptian or Red Sea exposure should watch the sanctions lists, because the network the UN describes crosses the UAE, Chad, Libya and Colombia.

Sudan once held 12 to 13 percent of the global sesame market, a UN Development Programme official said in September 2026. Its share has since fallen to six percent.

For shippers, Sudan’s war adds a second unstable shore to a strait that is already under pressure. Our Horn of Africa hub follows each of these threads across the region.

What Is Not Known

Even a Sudan war explained in detail leaves gaps, and no verified death toll for the war has been published. The UN human rights office counted at least 269 civilian deaths in Kordofan between 25 October and early December 2025 and said the real figure is likely higher.

The full chain of arms supply is not public. The UAE denies backing the RSF, and the public summary of the UN mission’s report does not say who supplied the army’s drones.

Whether Ethiopia is helping the RSF is not established. Security Council Report describes the claims only as allegations.

Whether the army will accept the 90-day truce is open, as is whether the RSF will agree to leave the cities it holds. Whether El Obeid holds against the RSF drone campaign is the most immediate military question.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Sudan war about?

The Sudan war explained in one line is a fight since April 2023 between two former allies, the army under General Burhan and the RSF under Hemedti. Both men face US sanctions.

Who backs the RSF and the Sudanese army?

Crisis Group names the UAE as the RSF’s chief sponsor, which the UAE denies, and Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Eritrea as backers of the army. UN investigators said in September 2026 that foreign suppliers strengthened the drone forces of both sides.

How many people have fled the war in Sudan?

The International Organization for Migration counts 8.6 million people displaced inside Sudan, as reported in September 2026. The UN refugee agency counted about 3.8 million Sudanese refugees and asylum seekers abroad at the end of 2025.

Is there a ceasefire in Sudan?

No ceasefire is in force, and Washington has proposed a 90-day humanitarian truce that the army has resisted. Burhan sent a message to President Trump on 15 October 2026 saying Sudan is committed to US-sponsored peace efforts.

World.content:

MEXICO · TRADE

Key Facts The country Mexico is Latin America’s second-largest economy and a major supplier of cars, electronics and machinery to the United States.

What happened On Thursday 15 October, the United Nations regional commission forecast that Mexico’s goods exports will rise 26% in 2026 to about US$835 billion.

The ranking Only Peru, at 30%, is forecast to grow faster, while the whole region is forecast to grow 20%.

The driver Computer hardware tied to artificial-intelligence investment leads the gain, with electronics exports forecast to grow more than 100%.

Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

Why it matters More Mexican cargo means more supply for US buyers, while the US-Mexico-Canada trade pact faces a review that could change tariff terms.

Mexico exports are on course to jump 26% this year, to about US$835 billion, according to a forecast published on Thursday 15 October. Only Peru, at 30%, is expected to grow faster among the region’s 33 economies.

The forecast comes from the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean, known as Cepal, a United Nations body based in Santiago, Chile. It matters to US readers because Mexico exports mostly go to the United States, and the jump rests on AI-linked computer hardware.

What Cepal Forecasts for the Region

Cepal’s annual trade outlook expects the value of Latin American and Caribbean goods exports to rise 20% in 2026. That would be the fastest growth since the post-pandemic rebound of 2021.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Prices are forecast to rise 11% and volumes 9%, which would be a sixth straight year of growth in volume. Twenty-eight of the region’s 33 countries are expected to export more, and 16 of them by double digits.

Imports are forecast to rise 16% as household spending recovers and companies buy more parts and machinery. Cepal’s executive secretary, José Manuel Salazar-Xirinachs, said the region still faces an uncertain geopolitical climate.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where Mexico Stands in the Ranking

Mexico exports are forecast at US$835.3 billion in 2026, a rise of 26% on 2025. That puts Mexico second in the region behind Peru, whose 30% gain comes mainly from metal exports.

Several of the region’s biggest gains come from raw materials, which benefit from higher prices. Mexico exports stand out because the growth comes from manufactured goods.

Cepal says Mexico’s manufactured exports grew more than 26% in the first half of 2026. Cepal credits the integration of North American supply chains and the move of production to Mexico.

Why AI Hardware Drives the Jump

Cepal says data-processing machinery and other goods linked to artificial-intelligence investment led the growth outside the car industry. Daniela García, who heads the commission’s trade division, said electronics exports are forecast to grow more than 100% and machinery more than 50%.

Mexico exports computer equipment to the US market, helped by production that moved closer to American customers in recent years. Monthly figures from Mexico’s statistics institute had already pointed this way, as The Rio Times reported when Mexican electronics sales doubled in August.

The share of the gain that comes from AI-related goods is not broken out. The rest comes from other factory exports that also grew in the first half.

The Trade Pact Review Hangs Over the Boom

The United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA, called T-MEC in Spanish) is the 2020 trade pact that lets most goods cross the three borders without tariffs. Cepal calls its coming review central for Mexico, since it covers trade, investment and the supply chains behind the export boom.

The commission fears Washington may not renew the pact on current terms, because it wants a smaller trade deficit. It also warns that separate US talks could split the pact in two, as our guide to Mexico’s place in North America explains.

Mexican press reports say US-Canada talks broke down in late August. The process could shift after the US midterm elections in November, while Cepal also cites unpredictable US trade policy and logistics problems.

What It Means for You

For US companies that buy Mexican-made electronics, machinery or parts, the forecast points to strong supply. It also points to exposure to the pact review, since any tariff change would hit the fastest-growing factories.

For investors watching Mexico, the figure shows strong trade while other forecasts are cooler. The International Monetary Fund on 13 October trimmed its Mexico growth forecast for next year to 1.8%.

What Is Not Known

The forecast is a projection, and the final 2026 figure for Mexico exports will come only after the year ends. How long the AI-hardware boom lasts is open.

The outcome of the USMCA review is open, as is whether Washington will agree to renew the pact. Cepal has not said how much of Mexico’s gain would be lost if tariff terms changed.

More: Mexico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much will Mexico’s exports grow in 2026?

Cepal forecasts Mexico’s goods exports will rise 26% in 2026 to about US$835 billion. Only Peru, at 30%, is forecast to grow faster.

What is Cepal?

Cepal is the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean, a United Nations body based in Santiago, Chile. It publishes the region’s main annual trade outlook.

Why are Mexico exports growing so fast?

Electronics and machinery tied to artificial-intelligence investment lead the gain, along with other factory goods. Cepal forecasts electronics exports to grow more than 100%.

What does this mean for the United States?

US buyers get more Mexican-made computer hardware and parts, but they also depend on the outcome of the USMCA review. A change in tariff terms would reach the same factories.

World.content:

COLOMBIA · ENERGY

Key Facts The country Colombia is a South American country of about 52 million people that gets most of its electricity from hydroelectric dams.

What happened On Thursday 15 October, Cali’s mayor and its city utility’s manager announced an offer to swap the city’s Celsia stake for the Salvajina dam.

The swap The utility would give up its shareholding in power producer Celsia Colombia and receive the whole Salvajina plant in return.

The money City officials say the deal needs no extra cash and no new borrowing, and valuations of both assets are still being updated.

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

The next step The city council must authorise the sale of the stake, and the two sides must still agree terms in talks that continue.

Still open Celsia has not published a public response, and neither the final price nor the closing date has been fixed.

The city of Cali wants to trade its Celsia stake for a hydroelectric dam, which would put a Colombian city into power generation. Mayor Alejandro Eder and Roger Mina, manager of the city-owned utility Emcali, announced the plan on Thursday 15 October.

Celsia is a listed Colombian energy company and the power arm of the conglomerate Grupo Argos, so a change among its shareholders matters to investors. El País Cali and 90 Minutos report that the Celsia stake would go in exchange for the Salvajina plant in the Cauca River basin.

What Cali Is Offering

Emcali, the municipal company that sells power, water and telephone services in Cali, owns a minority shareholding in Celsia Colombia. It has offered to give that Celsia stake to Celsia in exchange for the whole of the Salvajina hydroelectric plant.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Cali is Colombia’s third-largest city, with a large industrial and farming region around it. Mayor Eder, who runs the city government, said the plan would add a generating asset without new debt, according to El País Cali.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Colombia Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Salvajina Matters to Cali

Salvajina sits in the basin of the Cauca River, which runs through the Valle del Cauca region around Cali. The city says the plant also helps control floods, regulate river flow and supply drinking water, according to 90 Minutos.

Colombia’s wholesale power market, where prices can swing sharply when rain is scarce, is the risk the city wants to reduce. Mina told El País Cali that owning a plant would cut Emcali’s exposure to those purchases, including in an El Niño dry spell.

How the Swap Would Work

Under the proposal, Emcali would pay for Salvajina with its Celsia shares instead of cash. The city says no extra public money would be needed, according to 90 Minutos.

Mina described the offer as non-binding, meaning an expression of interest rather than a signed contract. Two valuations, one for the shares and one for the plant, will show whether the exchange is even or leaves a difference to settle.

The Approvals Still Needed

The Cali city council must authorise the sale of the Celsia stake, and the city has already sent the proposal to it. Public statements so far do not give a date for that vote.

The sale also follows Colombia’s Law 226 of 1995, which sets the rules for public bodies that sell their shares in companies. After valuations and talks, the two sides would still have to sign a binding offer and close the deal.

Celsia and the Power Market

Celsia generates power at plants across Colombia, and Salvajina was sold to a private owner about thirty years ago, according to the mayor. The swap would therefore return a dam to public hands while Celsia’s shareholder list changes.

Colombia relies on dams for most of its electricity, so dry-season risk is a live issue, as El Niño blackout fears in Bogotá show. The mayor said Colombian energy prices are set by the national government, not by the city.

What It Means for You

If you hold Colombian shares or follow the country through funds, the swap is a small, concrete change in who owns a major power company. It would not move prices overnight, since the deal is still an offer and a council vote lies ahead.

If you live in Cali or run a business there, the city says the goal is steadier power costs over time. Any effect on household bills is a future promise, not a decision.

What Is Not Known

Celsia has not published a response to the offer, and the final value of the swap has not been set. The mayor spoke of an offer accepted, while the utility manager called it a non-binding expression of interest.

The date of the council vote and of any closing is also open, and the council could change or reject the plan. Public statements so far come from the city and Emcali, not from Celsia.

More: Colombia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Cali offering to Celsia?

Emcali, the city-owned utility, offers its Celsia stake in return for the full Salvajina hydroelectric plant. City officials say it needs no extra cash or new debt.

Who must approve the swap?

The Cali city council must authorise the sale of the shares. The two sides must also finish valuations and sign a binding offer.

Is the deal final?

No, because so far Emcali has made a non-binding offer and talks continue. Celsia has not published its position.

Why does Cali want a dam?

City officials say a plant of its own would reduce Emcali’s exposure to volatile wholesale power prices. They also point to flood control and drinking water in the Cauca River basin.

World.content:

HONDURAS · POLITICS

Key Facts The country Honduras is a Central American nation of about 11 million people, with deep economic and security ties to the United States.

What happened Former president Manuel “Mel” Zelaya came home on Thursday 15 October after more than five weeks of medical care in Mexico.

Who he is Zelaya governed Honduras from 2006 until soldiers removed him in 2009, and he now coordinates the left-wing Libre party.

His health He says doctors discharged him on Wednesday 14 October, that he is not cured, and that treatment will last almost two years.

Why it matters Libre lost the presidency in January 2026 to Nasry Asfura, a conservative backed by US President Donald Trump, and Zelaya founded the party.

Still open How active a role his health allows, and what part he will play before the next presidential election in 2029.

The Honduras ex-president Manuel “Mel” Zelaya came back to the country on Thursday 15 October after more than five weeks of medical care in Mexico. He said doctors discharged him a day earlier, but that he is not cured.

Zelaya led Honduras from 2006 to 2009 and now heads Libre, the left-wing party opposing a government backed by US President Donald Trump. His return ends weeks of rumours about his health.

What Zelaya Said on Arrival

The Honduras ex-president spoke to the Honduran broadcaster HCH after coming home. “I am sick, I have not come back cured, I have come for treatment,” he said.

He told the station that the treatment is lighter than before and can be done in Honduras, but will last almost two years. He added that he will return to his duties in Libre as far as his health allows.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Honduras Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why He Was in Mexico

El Heraldo, a Honduran daily, reports that Zelaya had emergency surgery in early September to remove fluid around his heart. On 7 September he flew to Mexico for specialist tests to find the cause.

HCH described the problem as an inflammation and a fluid build-up in the pericardium, the membrane that wraps the heart. La Prensa, another Honduran daily, links it to pericarditis, and says Zelaya first resisted the operation.

How He Came Home

According to El Heraldo, Zelaya arrived at the Ramón Villeda Morales airport in San Pedro Sula, the country’s second-largest city. His doctor cleared him to continue treatment at home, and he said he was discharged on Wednesday 14 October.

La Prensa quotes him saying he did not slip out of hospital. He said that if he had gone home instead of accepting the operation, he “would not have woken up”.

The Death Rumours He Answered

False posts claiming that Zelaya had died on 2 October circulated while he was in Mexico, as an earlier Rio Times report described. La Prensa’s fact-checking desk, LP Verifica, called the claim false.

Zelaya joked that people had held his wake before he died, and he criticised political opponents who celebrated his illness. “I am here to continue this fight,” he told El Heraldo.

Back in Opposition to a Trump-Backed Government

Libre, short for Freedom and Refoundation, was founded by Zelaya after the 2009 coup and governed from 2022 under his wife, Xiomara Castro. It lost the November 2025 election, and Nasry Asfura of the conservative National Party took office on 27 January 2026.

Trump publicly backed Asfura days before that vote, as the Asfura profile explains. The Honduras ex-president told HCH that the Asfura government is failing.

What He Said About the Government

In a separate HCH interview Zelaya said the administration “has not been able to govern because it is listening to Honduras’s external interests”. He added that it pays attention to big companies that “only want to do business”.

He said the government is failing in every area. La Prensa adds that Zelaya wants Libre to prepare to win back power in the 2029 election.

Who Stands Beside Him in Libre

The Honduras ex-president is Libre’s general coordinator, the top post in the party. His deputy, Rixi Moncada, was the party’s presidential candidate in 2025 and finished third.

El Heraldo reports that Moncada visited him in Mexico and said on 11 October that he was stable. Zelaya praised her work as deputy coordinator when he spoke after his return.

What It Means for You

For US readers, Honduras is a major source of migration to the United States and a partner against drug gangs. Its politics shape both, so the health of the Honduras ex-president matters beyond his own party.

The return changes no policy and no travel conditions. The next presidential election is about three years away.

What Is Not Known

The Honduras ex-president says he has pericarditis, an inflammation of the membrane around the heart, but no medical report has been published. The hospital in Mexico where he was treated has not been named.

It is not known how many public events he will attend or whether he will formally lead Libre’s campaign for 2029. The Asfura government has not commented publicly on his remarks.

More: Honduras news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Mel Zelaya?

The Honduras ex-president, Manuel “Mel” Zelaya, was president of Honduras from 2006 until soldiers removed him in June 2009. He later founded the left-wing Libre party, which his wife Xiomara Castro led into government in 2022.

Why was Zelaya in Mexico?

He went to Mexico on 7 September for specialist tests after emergency surgery in Honduras to remove fluid from around his heart. Honduran media describe an inflammation and fluid build-up in the pericardium.

Is Zelaya cured?

No, the Honduras ex-president says he is still sick and has come home for treatment. He expects it to last almost two years.

Will Zelaya return to politics?

Yes, he says he will resume his duties as Libre’s general coordinator within the limits of his health. He praised deputy coordinator Rixi Moncada for doing her job well.

Who governs Honduras now?

Nasry Asfura of the conservative National Party has been president since 27 January 2026. He won the November 2025 election after public backing from Donald Trump.

Sources: El Heraldo, 15 October 2026; La Prensa, 15 October 2026; HCH, 15 October 2026; HCH, 15 October 2026.

PARAGUAY · BANKING

Key Facts The country Paraguay is a landlocked South American farm and hydropower exporter of about 6 million people, governed by President Santiago Peña.

What happened On Thursday 15 October the central bank’s national payment system had technical problems, and transfers from banking apps failed for a time.

Why it matters The Paraguay payment system links banks, finance companies and cooperatives, so a failure can stall payments for people and businesses at once.

Power Index Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 36.0 points (October 2026 edition).

The numbers The system moved an average of more than US$10 billion a month in 2025, and most banks cap one transfer at about US$1,750.

What it means for you Anyone paying or being paid in Paraguay, from expats to exporters, should keep a second way to pay in case a transfer fails.

Still open The cause of the failure, the number of users hit and whether any payment was lost have not been stated.

The Paraguay payment system, the central bank platform that moves money between the country’s banks, stalled on the morning of Thursday 15 October. The central bank, the Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP), flagged problems at about 8:12 local time and announced a fix at about 10:00.

For foreigners, the outage matters because most electronic bank transfers in Paraguay run through this one system. It also hit a central bank that senators are already pressing over how it supervised a bank called ueno.

What Happened on Thursday Morning

The BCP posted a notice on social media at about 8:12 local time. It said the Payment System of Paraguay, known as SIPAP, was having technical problems.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 36.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Última Hora, an Asunción daily, reported that the bank was working to restore service quickly and thanked the public for its patience. ABC Color, another Asunción daily, reported that users could not make transfers or payments from their banking apps.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Paraguay Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Paraguay Payment System Is Back

At about 10:00 the BCP announced on X that the service had been restored, ABC Color reported. The bank gave no cause and no figures for the disruption.

El Nacional, a third Paraguayan outlet, reported on Thursday that the Paraguay payment system had no set time for a return to normal. None of the three outlets said which banks or which kinds of transfers were hit.

What the Payment System Does

The Paraguay payment system is run by the BCP and links banks, finance companies, cooperatives and other public and private bodies, Última Hora reports. It is the country’s main channel for electronic transfers by individuals and companies.

ABC Color says the instant-payment side runs 24 hours a day, every day, with settlement in real time. Most banks cap one transfer at 10 million guaraníes (about US$1,750 at about 5,700 guaraníes to the US dollar on 16 October 2026).

How Much Money Moves Through It

According to BCP data cited by Última Hora, transfers through the Paraguay payment system averaged more than US$10 billion a month in 2025. That is a large flow for a country of about 6 million people.

A failure in such a hub is felt across the economy, because salaries, supplier invoices and rent can all pass through it. The reports describe disruption to transfers and app payments but give no count of failed operations.

A Showpiece System Under Strain

The BCP promotes its instant-payment service as a public digital platform for banks, cooperatives and fintech companies. It offers free transfers to the public, along with payment aliases and QR codes.

The BCP says the Organization of American States, a regional body, gave the service a regional award for public digital infrastructure. Thursday’s outage showed how many people depend on the service.

A Central Bank Already Under Pressure

The failure came a day after Senator Rafael Filizzola filed a motion urging President Peña to start removing the whole BCP board. The motion criticises how the bank supervised ueno bank.

Última Hora reported that the lower house had rejected a similar motion against BCP president Carlos Carvallo a day earlier. The Rio Times covers the dispute in what happens next for the Paraguay central bank board.

What It Means for You

For Americans living in Paraguay or paying Paraguayan suppliers, a transfer that fails in the morning should not be assumed to have gone through. A card, cash or a second bank account is a sensible back-up when the Paraguay payment system carries most payments.

For investors in Paraguayan banks and bonds, the BCP is both the payments operator and the banking regulator. Any confirmed cause, or a BCP report on the incident, would be the next detail to watch.

What Is Not Known

The BCP has not said what caused the technical problems or exactly when they began. It has also not said how many users, banks or payments were affected.

It is not known whether any transfers were delayed, duplicated or lost, or whether the BCP will publish an explanation. Nothing reported so far ties the outage to the dispute over the central bank board.

More: Paraguay news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened to the Paraguay payment system?

On Thursday 15 October the central bank said the national payment system had technical problems. Users reported that transfers and payments from banking apps failed.

Is the Paraguay payment system working again?

Yes, the BCP announced on X at about 10 a.m. that service had been restored, according to ABC Color. The bank has not published a cause.

What is SIPAP?

SIPAP is the Payment System of Paraguay, the platform run by the central bank that connects banks, finance companies, cooperatives and other bodies. It is the country’s main channel for electronic transfers.

How much money does it handle?

BCP data cited by Última Hora put the average at more than US$10 billion a month in 2025. That covers transfers between all connected institutions.

Does the outage affect visitors to Paraguay?

It could stall a bank transfer or app payment on the day, but the reports mention no effect on cards or travel. Visitors can carry some cash as a back-up.

World.content:

PANAMA · DISASTER RELIEF

Key Facts The country Panama uses the US dollar and runs the canal linking two oceans, led since July 2024 by conservative President José Raúl Mulino.

What happened On Thursday 15 October, Panama began paying quake relief to local governments: US$10,000 to each district representative and US$20,000 to each municipality.

The purpose Mayors and community leaders can buy water, medicine, food and household goods for families whose homes the 9 October earthquake damaged.

The limits The state audit office supervises the spending, and Mulino calls this a first payment, not the full sum.

The wider bill The Cabinet approved up to US$100 million for the emergency on 10 October, and the finance minister says spending is still far below that.

Power Index Panama ranks 11th of 14 in Panama ranks 11th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 34.2 points (October 2026 edition).

Still open How many local governments are paid, the total cost of the first round and the dates of later transfers.

Panama began paying earthquake relief to local governments on Thursday 15 October, with US$10,000 for each district representative and US$20,000 for each municipality. President José Raúl Mulino announced the Panama quake aid on X and said the state audit office would check the spending.

The payments matter to foreign readers because Panama runs on the US dollar and hosts many US visitors and retirees. They show how fast Panama quake aid reaches damaged towns after the 9 October quake and how tightly the government controls it.

What Panama Is Paying and to Whom

Mulino said on X that the money would be deposited on Thursday 15 October in the juntas comunales and the alcaldías. The juntas comunales are community boards led by the elected representatives of Panama’s districts, called corregimientos, and the alcaldías are the municipal governments.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Panama ranks 11th of 14 with 34.2 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (64); weakest: military means (11). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Each district representative receives US$10,000 and each alcaldía US$20,000 in Panama quake aid, according to La Estrella de Panamá. The paper said the money is for direct aid to people affected by the earthquake.

Telemetro reported that this is a first payment and that further money will follow gradually. The aim is to let mayors and representatives help residents whose homes were damaged or collapsed.

Mulino also said the sums do not necessarily equal the total that local governments will receive. He added that the money sent now is not everything, but that giving cannot run wild because the funds are public, Telemetro reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Panama Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Money Can Buy and Who Watches It

Telemetro reported that the Panama quake aid can cover drinking water, medicine, food, household goods and other urgent needs of affected families. Mulino stressed that this is not a piñata handing out cash, using the Spanish word for a party game to make his point.

The Contraloría General de la República, the state audit office, will supervise the spending closely, Mulino wrote. Comptroller General Anel Flores asked mayors and representatives to act with “prudence” when they handle the transferred money, Telemetro reported.

La Prensa reported that the comptroller also reviews each emergency purchasing contract after it is signed. Housing minister Jaime Jované’s ministry buys materials through online quotations under emergency rules.

How Hard the Quake Hit

The earthquake struck on Friday 9 October La Estrella reported. Its epicentre lay between Tonosí and Torío in Los Santos province.

Damage was reported in Coclé, Herrera, Los Santos and Veraguas provinces, and the Cabinet then approved a state of emergency. Canal Affairs Minister José Ramón Icaza said on Wednesday night that 3,696 people were in 45 shelters, up 855 from 2,841 on Tuesday.

The presidency said on Thursday that more than 465 tons of aid had reached households, including more than 16,000 food bags in 117 communities. Of 842 health facilities checked, 69 had minor damage, and about 600 official schools were damaged.

How Panama Is Paying for the Recovery

The Cabinet authorised up to US$100 million for Panama quake aid and repairs on Saturday 10 October, La Prensa reported. Finance Minister Felipe Chapman said the government is still very far from that ceiling.

Chapman said the state savings fund will not be touched, because using it requires damage above 0.5% of economic output, about US$450 million. The deficit target stays at 3.5% of GDP, and the ministry will not ask the Assembly to waive the fiscal responsibility law.

Two trusts hold the donations for Panama quake aid. The public trust at Banco Nacional takes multilateral donations and catastrophe insurance payouts, while the private trust sits at the Caja de Ahorros bank.

Community boards must file formal requests and show that each expense ties to quake damage to draw on the public trust. A website showing how public funds are used was announced, but no launch date was given.

What It Means for You

Tourism officials said on Wednesday 14 October that more than 90% of hotels are operating, at an average occupancy of 67%, La Estrella reported. Copa Airlines marketing director Marco Ocando said operations at Tocumen airport recovered within about 72 hours.

Gloria de León, head of the national tourism authority, said the most affected establishments are in Penonomé and Pedasí. Travellers heading to the interior should check official advice from the tourism authority and the civil protection agency Sinaproc first.

For investors in Panama, the finance ministry’s message is that the 3.5% deficit target holds and the savings fund stays untouched. Readers who want to give can use the private trust, which presidential adviser Eduardo Arango will coordinate.

What Is Not Known

Officials have not said how many community boards and municipalities will receive Panama quake aid or what the first round costs in total. They have also not given dates or amounts for the later transfers that Mulino mentioned.

No body has been named to audit the private donations trust, and it is unclear whether its accounts will be public. The final repair bill is also open, with Chapman saying only that it remains far from the US$100 million ceiling.

More: Panama news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much quake aid is Panama sending to local governments?

Panama quake aid starts at US$10,000 to each district representative and US$20,000 to each municipality as a first payment. President Mulino said more transfers may follow.

Who checks how the Panama quake aid is spent?

The Contraloría General, Panama’s state audit office, supervises the spending, and Comptroller General Anel Flores asked local officials to act with prudence. Mulino said the office will supervise the funds closely.

Can tourists still visit Panama after the earthquake?

Tourism officials say more than 90% of hotels are operating and the capital remains active. The worst damage is in interior areas such as Penonomé and Pedasí, so travellers should check official advice first.

How big is the budget for Panama quake aid?

The Cabinet authorised up to US$100 million on 10 October. Finance Minister Felipe Chapman said spending is still very far from that ceiling.

Where do donations to Panama go?

Public and multilateral donations go to a trust at Banco Nacional, and private gifts go to a second trust at the Caja de Ahorros bank. Presidential adviser Eduardo Arango coordinates the private contributions.

World.title: LatAm and Africa Football Odds, Weekend of 17 Oct
World.content:
Prediction Markets: Football

Key Facts —Prediction markets. Polymarket prices Flamengo at 54% and Palmeiras at 37% to win the Copa Libertadores, with US$35,312 traded. Flamengo were 42.5% a week ago, and the prices were read at 5:37 am ET on Friday 16 October 2026. —Liga MX. Kalshi, a US exchange regulated by the CFTC, gives Guadalajara 23% and América 19% to win the Clausura, on 542,549 contracts traded. Guadalajara host Tigres on Saturday 17 October at 7:07 pm ET. —Brazil. Polymarket has Flamengo at 61.5% and Palmeiras at 36% for the Série A title, with US$48,958 traded. Flamengo lead by one point, 64 to 63. —Africa. Polymarket makes Morocco the 33.5% favourite for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, ahead of Senegal at 15.4%. South Africa lead their qualifying group at 64.5%. —Match markets. No single-match market met our US$10,000 threshold for this weekend, so this edition leads with the title races. The next Libertadores semi-final legs are on 21 and 22 October.

Prediction markets make Flamengo the favourite, at 54%, to win the Copa Libertadores, the Champions League of South America. The Brazilian club drew 0–0 at Estudiantes in the first leg of the semi-final on Thursday 15 October.

For readers in the United States, this weekend is about title races rather than single matches. Mexico’s Liga MX plays its twelfth round, and Brazilian and Argentine clubs sit one leg away from a Libertadores final.

No single-match market reached our US$10,000 threshold this week, unlike last week’s edition. We therefore show the season markets, with their change over the past week, and the fixtures that matter most to them.

What Prediction Markets Say

A price of 54% means a contract that pays US$1 if Flamengo win the Libertadores costs about 54 US cents. Prices are bets by traders, not forecasts by The Rio Times.

Polymarket counts volume in US dollars, while Kalshi counts contracts worth up to US$1 each. Many of these markets have only tens of thousands of dollars traded, so a single large bet can move a price.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on AFCON 2027 Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

This Weekend’s Matches

No match-level market reached the threshold, so there are no win-draw-lose prices to report. The fixtures below are the ones that bear most directly on the title markets, with kick-off in Mexico City and in New York.

Mexico City is on UTC−6 all year, while New York is on Eastern Daylight Time until 1 November. Mexican kick-offs are therefore two hours later in ET.

Liga MX Apertura, round 12

Chivas play Tigres on Saturday 17 October at 5:07 pm in Guadalajara (7:07 pm ET), at the Estadio Akron. Guadalajara are fourth with 19 points and lead the Kalshi Clausura market.

León host América on Saturday at 7:00 pm in León (9:00 pm ET). América lead the table with 21 points, with one postponed match still to play, according to Fox Sports México.

Toluca host Atlético de San Luis on Saturday at 7:00 pm in Toluca (9:00 pm ET), at the Estadio Nemesio Díez. Toluca have 20 points, level with Querétaro, and lost 3–2 to Tigres in round 11.

File photo: Tigres and Chivas players in an earlier league meeting. This is not from this weekend’s match.

Monterrey host Pachuca on Sunday 18 October at 7:00 pm in Monterrey (9:00 pm ET), at the Estadio BBVA. Friday’s round-12 games include Necaxa vs Atlas and Tijuana vs Puebla.

Cruz Azul drew 3–3 with Pumas in round 11 and have 17 points. They face FC Juárez on Saturday evening in Mexico City.

Brazil and the Libertadores

In Série A round 31, Palmeiras visit Athletico-PR on Saturday 17 October at 7:30 pm in Brasília (6:30 pm ET). Flamengo visit Bahia on Sunday 18 October at 6:30 pm in Brasília (5:30 pm ET), according to GC Mais.

Palmeiras won the first leg 2–1 at Fluminense at the Maracanã on Wednesday 14 October. Flaco López and Marlon Freitas scored for Palmeiras, and Wesley Natã replied in stoppage time.

Palmeiras host Fluminense at the Nubank Parque on Wednesday 21 October. Flamengo host Estudiantes at the Maracanã on Thursday 22 October at 9:30 pm in Brasília (8:30 pm ET).

The winners of the two ties meet in the final on Saturday 28 November at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo. Both Brazilian sides therefore have a league game this weekend and a semi-final return in midweek.

Latin America Title Races

Mexico: a crowded Liga MX table

Polymarket’s Apertura winner market, with US$106,824 traded, prices América at 22.5%, Guadalajara at 16.5%, Toluca at 14.1% and Cruz Azul at 13.5%. América gained 6 points in a week, while Toluca fell 9.3 points from 23.4% after the loss to Tigres.

Kalshi’s Clausura champion market has 542,549 contracts traded and prices Guadalajara at 23%, América at 19%, León at 11% and Cruz Azul at 10%. Toluca and Santos Laguna are both at 6%.

The Clausura is the second tournament of the season, so this market looks far ahead. It still shows which clubs traders rate over the full season.

Polymarket’s market for second place in the Apertura puts América at 21.5%, Chivas at 17.5%, Toluca at 16.1% and Cruz Azul at 12%, with US$48,081 traded. These individual-finish markets are thinner than the title markets.

For the 2026–27 top scorer, Juan Brunetta leads at 15.2%, up from 10% a week ago, ahead of Paulinho at 9% and Juninho at 6%, with US$28,658 traded. Club América are 32.5% in the market for the largest goal difference, ahead of Toluca at 26.5%, on US$12,177.

Brazil: Flamengo lead by one point

Flamengo lead the Série A with 64 points after a 1–0 win over Fluminense on Sunday 11 October, with Carrascal scoring in the 52nd minute. Palmeiras are second with 63 points after a 4–1 win over Corinthians.

Polymarket prices Flamengo at 61.5% and Palmeiras at 36% for the title, with US$48,958 traded. A week ago Flamengo were 68.5% and Palmeiras 30%, so the gap has narrowed by about 13 points.

At the bottom, Corinthians (32 points) and Internacional (32) are 16th and 17th, and Grêmio (31) are 18th after a 1–1 draw between Grêmio and Internacional. Corinthians have now lost eight games in a row, according to O Povo.

Polymarket’s relegation market, with US$18,156 traded, lists Remo at 97.9% and Chapecoense at 97.5%. Internacional are at 61.3%, Grêmio at 51% and Corinthians at 49.5%.

Copa Libertadores: Flamengo 54%, Palmeiras 37%

Flamengo are 54% on Polymarket, up from 42.5% a week ago. Palmeiras are at 37%, up from 26.5%, and Estudiantes de La Plata are at 19.8%.

The goalless draw in La Plata keeps the Flamengo–Estudiantes tie open for the Maracanã. Palmeiras’ 2–1 away win explains their rise, because a draw at home would now be enough for them.

Relegation elsewhere in the region

In Colombia’s Primera A, Polymarket prices Boyacá Chicó at 81% and Jaguares at 62.5% to be relegated, with US$20,992 traded. In Peru’s Liga 1, UTC Cajamarca are at 68%, Deportivo Moquegua at 54.5% and FC Cajamarca at 43.5%, on US$19,607.

These are “teams relegated” markets, so several clubs can each be priced above 50%. Peru’s market has under US$20,000 traded, so its prices can swing on a single order.

Africa

Every African market above our threshold this week is about the Africa Cup of Nations, the 2027 edition of which is hosted jointly by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda under the name Pamoja. No African league or club-competition market met the US$10,000 line.

Polymarket’s tournament winner market has US$16,790 traded. It prices Morocco at 33.5%, Senegal at 15.4%, Ivory Coast at 11.2%, Egypt at 7.8%, South Africa at 7.5% and Ghana at 6.6%.

The group-winner markets run until 31 March 2027, according to Polymarket. South Africa are 64.5% to win Group D, ahead of Guinea at 29.5%, after beating Eritrea 5–0 to lead the group with six points, according to EWN Sport.

Egypt are 69.5% in Group B, ahead of Angola at 26.5%. Mali are 60.5% in Group K, Burkina Faso 58.5% in Group F, Tunisia 56.5% in Group H and Nigeria 61.5% in Group L.

Each of these group markets has between US$10,663 and US$15,985 traded. That is small next to the Liga MX and Libertadores books.

What It Means for US Readers

Mexican and Brazilian clubs have large followings among Mexican-American and Brazilian-American fans. The prices give those fans, and anyone new to the sport, a quick read on who traders think will win.

Kalshi is a US exchange regulated by the CFTC. We link to our own coverage and to public data only, and we do not offer betting tips or links to betting sites.

For the week ahead, the Libertadores return legs on 21 and 22 October are the most likely events to move prices. Our daily Latin America Sports Daily covers the results.

Our live boards are on the Latin America odds hub and the Africa odds hub. They update through the day, so the prices there may differ from those read here.

What Is Not Known

We do not have confirmed line-ups or injury lists for round 12, and weather at the Mexican grounds could change tempo. Fixtures are also subject to change.

Prices in thin markets can move on a single trade, and Série A sides often rotate players around Libertadores games. Both effects can shift the title markets before Sunday night.

Polymarket prices Morocco at 33.5% to win the tournament, ahead of Senegal at 15.4% and Ivory Coast at 11.2%. The market has US$16,790 traded, so the prices are a rough guide.

World.content:
One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

COLOMBIA · MARKETS

Key Facts The country Colombia is a South American country and a long-standing US partner, and its capital, Bogotá, gives this power group its name.

What happened Grupo Energía Bogotá (GEB), a power and gas group, raised 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) in short-term notes on Thursday 15 October.

The notes They are fixed-rate peso notes that mature in 180 or 364 days and were sold by auction on the Colombian stock exchange.

The programme This was the first sale under a programme of up to 2.5 trillion pesos (about US$785 million) in bonds and short-term notes.

The US link GEB has started the process of listing its shares in the United States, so the sale shows how local investors price the company.

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

The catch The interest rate and the number of bids have not been published, and the notes are priced in pesos.

A Colombia power group, Grupo Energía Bogotá (GEB), raised 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) from investors on Thursday 15 October 2026. The group sold short-term notes at an auction on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC), the country’s stock exchange.

For US investors the sale tests demand for a company that has begun the process of listing its shares in the United States. The notes are priced in pesos, so a dollar-based buyer would carry currency risk.

What Grupo Energía Bogotá Sold

The Colombia power group placed 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) in commercial paper, which is short-term company debt that is repaid within a year. La República and Portafolio, two Colombian business outlets, both reported the full amount on Thursday.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The initial offer was 250 billion pesos (about US$79 million), with an option to add 150 billion pesos (about US$47 million) if demand ran higher. The final sum of 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) shows the group used the full option.

The notes mature in 180 or 364 days and pay a fixed rate, according to the offer notice reported on Wednesday. Each note has a face value of 1 million pesos (about US$314), so ordinary investors could take part.

How the Auction Worked

The BVC ran a Dutch auction, in which bids are ranked from the lowest to the highest rate. Colombia’s Finance Ministry sets a maximum rate that stays hidden from bidders, Portafolio reported.

Payment is due on Friday 16 October 2026. Valores Bancolombia led the placement alongside BBVA Valores, BTG Pactual and Corredores Davivienda, Portafolio reported.

The investment-banking unit of the Colombian lender Bancolombia structured and coordinated the offer, La República reported. The law firm Holland & Knight Colombia advised GEB on legal matters.

A First Test for a Larger Debt Programme

The sale is the first under a programme allowing up to 2.5 trillion pesos (about US$785 million) in bonds and commercial paper. About 2.1 trillion pesos (about US$659 million) remains available, Portafolio reported.

La República reported that the previous issue dated from 2022, and GEB president Juan Ricardo Ortega welcomed the return to the capital market. He said the group wants to expand its capacity to finance regional energy infrastructure.

Andrés Restrepo Montoya, the BVC’s general manager, said the revival of commercial paper strengthens a short-term financing option that fits companies’ needs. The exchange hosted the auction on its main market.

Who Grupo Energía Bogotá Is

The Colombia power group is active in electricity and natural gas, with operations in Colombia, Peru, Brazil and Guatemala, according to its website. Readers can follow the group on its Rio Times Company Intelligence profile.

Fitch Ratings said in May that the Colombia power group is expanding its power-transmission business in Brazil, which requires new debt, Valora Analitik reported. Fitch expected dividends from its Brazilian joint venture to help bring borrowing down from 2027.

Fitch also pointed to about US$2 billion of debt falling due in 2027 and 2028, which it said weighs on financial flexibility. Short-term notes like Thursday’s give the Colombia power group another place to borrow.

Where the Money Goes and How It Is Rated

The Colombia power group said all proceeds go to general corporate purposes, Valora Analitik reported. Until the cash is spent, it may sit in low-risk, highly liquid financial instruments.

Fitch Ratings Colombia rates the notes F1+(col) and the whole programme AAA(col), according to the offer notice that Portafolio reported. Both ratings are on Fitch’s Colombian national scale, not its global scale.

What It Means for You

US investors cannot simply buy these notes from home, because buyers must be clients of an authorised Colombian broker and pass its anti-money-laundering checks. An earlier Rio Times report on the auction notice explains how a Colombian investor places an order.

It shows how Colombian investors price a utility that wants American shareholders, since Valora Analitik reported the US listing process has begun. The notes are in pesos, at about 3,185 to the US dollar on 16 October 2026, so dollar holders face currency risk.

What Is Not Known

The cut-off interest rates for the 180-day and 364-day notes have not been published. The number of bids and the split of the 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) between the two maturities are also not public.

No date for the US share listing has been announced. GEB has also not said when it will return to the market with bonds under the programme.

More: Colombia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Grupo Energía Bogotá sell on 15 October?

The Colombia power group placed 400 billion pesos (about US$126 million) of commercial paper on the Colombian stock exchange. The notes mature in 180 or 364 days.

What is commercial paper?

Commercial paper is short-term debt that a company sells to investors and repays within a year. Here the notes run for 180 or 364 days.

Can US investors buy the notes?

Buyers had to be clients of an authorised Colombian broker and pass its anti-money-laundering checks. The notes are priced in pesos, so dollar holders face currency risk.

Why does the Colombia power group sale matter abroad?

The Colombia power group has begun a US share listing process, so the sale shows how local investors view it. The company has given no date for the listing.

How much more can the company borrow under the programme?

The programme allows up to 2.5 trillion pesos (about US$785 million). About 2.1 trillion pesos (about US$659 million) remains after this sale.
